title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ وَشَمْسِ الدِّينِ
titleEn: Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn, continued: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan
part: Night 21 · The Tale of Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 154–164 (Night 21, continuing directly from nights-20), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 21 follows Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī in Basra, where he marries the vizier's daughter; on the same night in Cairo his brother Shams al-Dīn marries too, and each has a child — Nūr al-Dīn a son, Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, of astonishing beauty. Nūr al-Dīn succeeds his father-in-law as vizier, raises the boy, and on his deathbed gives him five counsels and a sealed letter naming his Egyptian kin. Disgraced by a jealous successor, Ḥasan flees to his father's tomb, where a jinniyya and an ʿifrīt, comparing him with the vizier's daughter in Cairo, tell of her forced marriage to a hunchback groom. Verse is copied as printed, and pointed by us only where the print has no marks. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْحَادِيَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-ḥādiyatu wa-al-ʿishrūna qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu
sentences.l: So when was the night the-first and-the-twenty, she-said: It-reached-me, O king the-fortunate,
sentences.i: When it was the twenty-first night, she said: It has reached me, fortunate king,
sentences.n: Arabic counts "the first and the twenty", units before tens.

sentences.t: أَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ قَامَ لَهُ وَرَحَّبَ بِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ قُمِ ادْخُلْ هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةَ عَلَى زَوْجَتِكَ وَفِي غَدٍ أَطْلَعُ بِكَ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ وَأَرْجُولَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ كُلَّ خَيْرٍ
sentences.tr: anna al-wazīra qāma lahu wa-raḥḥaba bihi wa-qāla lahu qumi udkhul hādhihi al-layla ʿalā zawjatika wa-fī ghadin aṭlaʿu bika ilā al-sulṭāni wa-arjūlaka min Allāhi kulla khayrin
sentences.l: that the vizier arose for-him and welcomed him, and said to-him: Arise, enter this night upon your-wife; and in tomorrow I-go-up with-you to the Sultan, and-I-hope for-you from God every good.
sentences.i: that the vizier rose for him and welcomed him, and said to him: Arise, go in to your wife this night, and tomorrow I shall take you up to the Sultan, and I hope for every good for you from God.
sentences.n: دَخَلَ عَلَى, "enter upon", is the usual idiom for going in to a bride on the wedding night. In وَأَرْجُولَكَ the verb and لَكَ are run together in the print: "and I hope for you".

sentences.t: فَقَامَ نُورُالدِّينِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى زَوْجَتِهِ بِنْتِ الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma Nūru al-Dīni wa-dakhala ʿalā zawjatihi binti al-wazīri
sentences.l: So arose Nūr al-Dīn and entered upon his-wife, the-daughter of-the-vizier.
sentences.i: So Nūr al-Dīn rose and went in to his wife, the vizier's daughter.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ نُورِالدِّينِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri Nūri al-Dīni
sentences.l: This is what was of the-affair of-Nūr al-Dīn.
sentences.i: So much for Nūr al-Dīn.
sentences.n: This is the storyteller's hinge: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ ... "so much for ...", then وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ ... "and as for ..." turns to the other party.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَاكَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ أَخِيهِ فَإِنَّهُ غَابَ مَعَ السُّلْطَانِ مُدَّةً فِىالسَّفَرِ وَرَجَعَ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ أَخَاهُ فَسَأَلَ عَنْهُ الْخُدَّامَ فَقَالُوا لَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mākāna min amri akhīhi fa-innahu ghāba maʿa al-sulṭāni muddatan fī al-safari wa-rajaʿa fa-lam yajid akhāhu fa-saʾala ʿanhu al-khuddāma fa-qālū lahu
sentences.l: And as for what-was of the-affair of-his-brother, then-indeed-he was-absent with the Sultan a-while in-the-journey, and returned, and-not he-found his-brother; so he-asked about-him the-servants, and-they-said to-him:
sentences.i: As for what befell his brother: Shams al-Dīn had been away with the Sultan for a time on a journey, and when he returned he did not find his brother; so he asked the servants about him, and they said to him:
sentences.n: The edition runs some words together (مَاكَانَ, فِىالسَّفَرِ); the spelling is kept as printed.

sentences.t: مِنْ يَوْمِ سَافَرْتَ مَعَ السُّلْطَانِ رَكِبَ بَغْلَتَهُ بِعُدَّةِ الْمَوْكِبِ وَقَالَ أَنَا رَائِحٌ نَاحِيَةَ الْقَلْيُوبِيَّةِ أَغِيبُ يَوْمًا أَوْيَوْمَيْنِ فَإِنَّ صَدْرِي ضَاقَ وَلَا أَحَدٌ يَتْبَعُنِي
sentences.tr: min yawmi sāfarta maʿa al-sulṭāni rakiba baghlatahu bi-ʿuddati al-mawkibi wa-qāla anā rāʾiḥun nāḥiyata al-Qalyūbiyyati aghību yawman awyawmayni fa-inna ṣadrī ḍāqa wa-lā aḥadun yatbaʿunī
sentences.l: From the-day you-travelled with the Sultan, he-rode his-mule with-the-equipment of-the-procession and said: I am going toward Qalyūbiyya; I-am-absent a-day or-two-days, for indeed my-chest has-grown-tight, and not anyone follows-me.
sentences.i: Ever since the day you set out with the Sultan, he mounted his mule with the full gear of a procession and said: I am off toward Qalyubiyya; I shall be away a day or two, for my heart is oppressed, and no one is to follow me.
sentences.n: The servants speak to Shams al-Dīn, hence سَافَرْتَ, "you travelled". Qalyūbiyya is the district north of Cairo. ضَاقَ صَدْرِي, "my chest grew tight", means "I felt oppressed". I read بِعُدَّةِ as ʿudda, "equipment, gear" (the mule decked out as for a procession); بِعِدَّةِ, "with a number of", is the other possibility.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ يَوْمِ خُرُوجِهِ إِلَى هَذَا الْيَوْمِ لَمْ نَسْمَعْ لَهُ خَبَرًا
sentences.tr: wa-min yawmi khurūjihi ilā hādhā al-yawmi lam nasmaʿ lahu khabaran
sentences.l: And from the-day of-his-going-out to this day, not we-have-heard of-him news.
sentences.i: and from the day he went out until today we have heard no news of him.

sentences.t: فَتَشَوَّشَ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ عَلَى فِرَاقِ أَخِيهِ وَاغْتَمَّ غَمًّا شَدِيدًا لِفَقْدِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-tashawwasha Shamsu al-Dīni ʿalā firāqi akhīhi wa-ightamma ghamman shadīdan li-faqdihi
sentences.l: So was-troubled Shams al-Dīn over the-parting-from his-brother, and grieved a-grief severe on-account-of his-loss.
sentences.i: Shams al-Dīn was distraught at parting from his brother, and grieved bitterly over losing him.
sentences.n: تَشَوَّشَ, "to be disturbed, thrown into confusion", is a later, colloquial-leaning verb, not a classical one.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ مَا هُوَ إِلَّا مِمَّا نَهَرْتُهُ فِي تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةِ أَخَذَ عَلَى خَاطِرِهِ وَخَرَجَ مُسَافِرًا فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ أُرْسِلَ خَلْفَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla fī nafsihi mā huwa illā mimmā naharthu fī tilka al-laylati akhadha ʿalā khāṭirihi wa-kharaja musāfiran fa-lā budda an ursila khalfahu
sentences.l: And he-said in himself: It is nothing but from-what I-rebuked-him in that night; he-took upon his-heart and went-out travelling; so no escape that I-send behind-him.
sentences.i: And he said to himself: This can only be because of what I scolded him for on that night; he took it to heart and went out travelling. I must send after him.
sentences.n: أَخَذَ عَلَى خَاطِرِهِ, "took upon his heart", means "took offence".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَلَعَ وَأَعْلَمَ السُّلْطَانَ وَكَتَبَ بِطَاقَاتٍ وَأَرْسَلَ الْبَرِيدَ إِلَى نُوَّابِهِ فِي جَمِيعِ الْبِلَادِ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭalaʿa wa-aʿlama al-sulṭāna wa-kataba biṭāqātin wa-arsala al-barīda ilā nuwwābihi fī jamīʿi al-bilādi
sentences.l: Then he-went-up and informed the Sultan, and wrote slips, and sent the-post to his-deputies in all the-lands.
sentences.i: Then he went up to the palace and informed the Sultan, and he wrote letters and sent the post to his deputies in every land.
sentences.n: بِطَاقَات is one word (biṭāqa, "slip, note"), not بِـ plus a noun.

sentences.t: وَنُورُا لدِّينِ فِي مُدَّةِ الْعِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا الَّتِي غَابُوهَا قَطَعَ بِلَادًا بَعِيدَةً
sentences.tr: wa-Nūru al-Dīni fī muddati al-ʿishrīna yawman allatī ghābūhā qaṭaʿa bilādan baʿīdatan
sentences.l: And Nūr al-Dīn, in the-period of-the-twenty days which they-were-absent-it, crossed lands distant.
sentences.i: And Nūr al-Dīn, during the twenty days of their absence, had crossed distant lands.
sentences.n: The print splits the name as نُورُا لدِّينِ; read Nūr al-Dīn (the lām of the article is silent before the dāl). غَابُوهَا gives غَابَ an object, "the days they were absent through", a loose Middle Arabic use; who "they" are (the searchers, or the absent brothers) is not clear.

sentences.t: فَفَتَّشُوا وَلَمْ يَقَعُوالَهُ عَلَى خَبَرٍ فَرَجَعُوا وَأَيِسَ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ مِنْ أَخِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-fattashū wa-lam yaqaʿū lahu ʿalā khabarin fa-rajaʿū wa-ayisa Shamsu al-Dīni min akhīhi
sentences.l: So they-searched, and not they-lighted for-him upon news; so they-returned; and despaired Shams al-Dīn of his-brother.
sentences.i: They searched but found no news of him, and returned; and Shams al-Dīn gave up hope of his brother.
sentences.n: وَأَيِسَ is ayisa, a by-form of yaʾisa, "he despaired" (the root also appears as أيس in the old lexica).

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَقَدْ فَرَّطْتُ فِي أَخِي بِكَلَامِي لَهُ عَلَى زَوَاجِ الْأَوْلَادِ قَلَّ ذَلِكَ أَنْ يَكُونَ وَمَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا مِنْ قِلَّةِ عَقْلِي وَعَدَمِ تَدْبِيرِي
sentences.tr: wa-qāla laqad farraṭtu fī akhī bi-kalāmī lahu ʿalā zawāji al-awlādi qalla dhālika an yakūna wa-mā kāna dhālika illā min qillati ʿaqlī wa-ʿadami tadbīrī
sentences.l: And he-said: Indeed I-was-remiss regarding my-brother through my-speech to-him about the-marriage of-the-children. Rare was that, that it be; and not was that except from littleness of-my-intellect and absence of-my-management.
sentences.i: And he said: I have failed my brother by speaking to him about marrying off the children. Such a thing is rare; it came only from my want of sense and my lack of foresight.
sentences.n: قل ذلك ان يكون is obscure. I read قَلَّ ذَلِكَ أَنْ يَكُونَ as "that seldom happens"; the print may also stand for a corrupted قَالَ, so treat the sense of this clause as uncertain. فَرَّطَ فِي means "to be remiss about, to fail"; بِـ in بِكَلَامِي marks the cause, "through my speaking".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ مُدَّةٍ يَسِيرَةٍ خَطَبَ بِنْتَ رَجُلٍ مِنْ تُجَّارِ مِصْرَ وَكَتَبَ كِتَابَهُ وَدَخَلَ بِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda muddatin yasīratin khaṭaba binta rajulin min tujjāri Miṣra wa-kataba kitābahu wa-dakhala bihā
sentences.l: Then after a-while small he-betrothed the-daughter of-a-man from merchants-of Egypt, and wrote his-contract, and entered with-her.
sentences.i: Then, after a short while, he asked for the hand of the daughter of one of the merchants of Egypt, drew up his marriage contract, and consummated the marriage with her.
sentences.n: دَخَلَ بِهَا, "entered with her", is the idiom for consummating a marriage: the verb itself selects بِـ.

sentences.t: وَقَدِ اتَّفَقَ أَنَّ لَيْلَةَ دُخُولِ شَمْسِ الدِّينِ عَلَى زَوْجَتِهِ كَانَتْ لَيْلَةَ دُخُولِ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلَى زَوْجَتِهِ بِنْتِ وَزِيرِالْبَصْرَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qadi ittafaqa anna laylata dukhūli Shamsi al-Dīni ʿalā zawjatihi kānat laylata dukhūli Nūri al-Dīni ʿalā zawjatihi binti wazīri al-Baṣrati
sentences.l: And it-so-happened that the-night of-entering of-Shams al-Dīn upon his-wife was the-night of-entering of-Nūr al-Dīn upon his-wife, the-daughter of-the-vizier-of-Basra.
sentences.i: And it so happened that the night Shams al-Dīn went in to his wife was the very night Nūr al-Dīn went in to his wife, the daughter of the vizier of Basra.

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ بِإِرَادَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى حَتَّى يُنَفِّذَ حُكْمَهُ فِي خَلْقِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika bi-irādati Allāhi taʿālā ḥattā yunaffidha ḥukmahu fī khalqihi
sentences.l: And that was by-the-will of-God, Exalted, until he-carries-out his-decree among his-creation.
sentences.i: And that was by the will of God Almighty, so that He might carry out His decree among His creatures.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ كَمَا قَالَاهُ وَحَمَلُوا النِّسَاءُ مِنْهُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna kamā qālāhu wa-ḥamalū al-nisāʾu minhumā
sentences.l: And it-was as the-two-said-it, and they-conceived the-women by-the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: And it came about as the two had said, and the women conceived by them.
sentences.n: The plural verb before its plural subject (حَمَلُوا النِّسَاءُ) is a Middle Arabic feature; classical Arabic would say حَمَلَتِ النِّسَاءُ. "As the two had said" looks back to the brothers' earlier agreement to marry their children to each other.

sentences.t: وَقَدْوَضَعَتْ زَوْجَةُ شَمْسِ الدِّينِ وَزِيرِ مِصْرَ بِنْتًا لَا يُرَى فِي مِصْرَ أَحْسَنُ مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qadwaḍaʿat zawjatu Shamsi al-Dīni wazīri Miṣra bintan lā yurā fī Miṣra aḥsanu minhā
sentences.l: And-had-given-birth the-wife of-Shams al-Dīn, the-vizier-of Egypt, to-a-daughter, not is-seen in Egypt more-beautiful than-her.
sentences.i: And the wife of Shams al-Dīn, the vizier of Egypt, bore a daughter, than whom none lovelier was to be seen in Egypt.

sentences.t: وَوَضَعَتْ زَوْجَةُ نُورِالدِّينِ وَلَدًا ذَكَرًا لَايُرَى فِي زَمَانِهِ أَحْسَنُ مِنْهُ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهِ الشَّاعِرَا شِ—رًا
sentences.tr: wa-waḍaʿat zawjatu Nūri al-Dīni waladan dhakaran lāyurā fī zamānihi aḥsanu minhu kamā qāla fīhi al-shāʿirā shiʿran
sentences.l: And gave-birth the-wife of-Nūr al-Dīn to-a-boy, a-male, not is-seen in his-time more-beautiful than-him, as said of-him the-poet, in-verse:
sentences.i: And Nūr al-Dīn's wife bore a boy, a male child, than whom none handsomer was to be seen in his time, as the poet said of him in verse:
sentences.n: The print has الشَّاعِرَا with a stray final alif, and the word for "in verse" appears as ش—را, with a dash where the ʿayn should be; read shiʿran. Both look like printing slips, and I keep them as printed.

sentences.t:
وَمُهَفْهَفٍ مِنْ شَعْرِهِ وَجَبِينِهِ * تَغْدُو الْوَرَى فِي ظُلْمَةٍ وَضِي
لَا تُنْكِرُوا الخَالَ الَّذِي فِي خَدِّهِ * كُلُّ الشَّقِيقِ بِنُقْطَةٍ سَوْدَاءِ
sentences.tr:
wa-muhafhafin min shaʿrihi wa-jabīnihi * taghdū al-warā fī ẓulmatin wa-ḍī
lā tunkirū al-khāla alladhī fī khaddihi * kullu al-shaqīqi bi-nuqṭatin sawdāʾi
sentences.l:
And a-slender-one, from his-hair and his-brow, * the-creatures go-about in a-darkness and-ḍī;
Do-not deny the-mole which is on his-cheek: * all the-anemone is with-a-spot black.
sentences.i: A slender-waisted youth: from his hair and his brow the creatures walk in darkness and in light. Do not deny the mole upon his cheek: every anemone is marked with a black spot.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse and the pointing is kept as printed. وَضِي at the end of the first line is cut short in the print; it is presumably وَضِيَاءٍ, "and radiance" (the line rhymes in -āʾ with سَوْدَاءِ): dark hair, bright brow. شَقِيق is the anemone, red with a black centre, a stock image for a cheek with a beauty spot. تَغْدُو الْوَرَى has a feminine verb with الْوَرَى, "mankind", which is a collective.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ آخَرُ شِ—رًا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla ākharu shiʿran
sentences.l: And said another, in-verse:
sentences.i: And another said, in verse:

sentences.t:
اِنْ جِيءَ بِالْحُسْنِ كَيْ يُقَاسَ بِهِ * يَنْكُسُ الْحُسْنُ رَسَهُ خَجِلًا
اَوْ قِيلَ يَا حُسْنُ هَلْ رَأَيْتَ كَذَا * فَقَالَ اَمَّا كَذَا رَأَيْتُ فَلَا
sentences.tr:
in jīʾa bi-al-ḥusni kay yuqāsa bihi * yankusu al-ḥusnu raʾsahu khajilan
aw qīla yā ḥusnu hal raʾayta kadhā * fa-qāla ammā kadhā raʾaytu fa-lā
sentences.l:
If is-brought with-the-beauty so-that it-be-measured by-him, * bows the-beauty its-head (printed رَسَهُ), ashamed;
or it-is-said: O beauty, have-you-seen the-like-of-this? * then-it-says: As-for the-like-of-this, I-have-seen, then no.
sentences.i: If Beauty itself were brought to be measured against him, Beauty would bow its head in shame; or if it were asked, "O Beauty, have you ever seen the like?", it would answer, "As for the like of this, I have never seen it."
sentences.n: The edition prints رَسَهُ for رَأْسَهُ, "his head", dropping the hamza; read raʾsahu. فَلَا at the end is a flat "no": the final clause says that Beauty has seen nothing like him.

sentences.t: فَسَمَّاهُ بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ وَفَرِحَ بِهِ جَدُّهُ وَزِيرُالْبَصْرَةِ وَصَنَعَ الْوَلَائِمَ وَعَمِلَ أَسْمِطَا تَصْلُحُ لِأَوْلَادِ الْمُلُوكِ
sentences.tr: fa-sammāhu Badra al-Dīni Ḥasanun wa-fariḥa bihi jadduhu wazīru al-Baṣrati wa-ṣanaʿa al-walāʾima wa-ʿamila asmiṭā taṣluḥu li-awlādi al-mulūki
sentences.l: So he-named-him Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and rejoiced in-him his-grandfather, the-vizier-of-Basra, and made the-banquets, and prepared spreads fit for-the-sons-of the-kings.
sentences.i: So he named him Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and the boy's grandfather, the vizier of Basra, rejoiced in him, and gave banquets, and had spreads laid such as befit the sons of kings.
sentences.n: اسمطا is the plural of سِمَاط (a laid table, a banquet spread), printed with a final alif where the classical plural أَسْمِطَة would end in ـة; the verb تَصْلُحُ is feminine singular, as a plural of things regularly takes.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ وَزِيرَالْبَصْرَةِ أَخَذَ مَعَهُ نُورَالدِّينِ وَطَلَعَ بِهِ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ قُدَّامَهُ قَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna wazīra al-Baṣrati akhadha maʿahu Nūra al-Dīni wa-ṭalaʿa bihi ilā al-sulṭāni fa-lammā aqbala quddāmahu qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: Then indeed the-vizier-of-Basra took with-him Nūr al-Dīn, and went-up with-him to the-Sultan; and when he-came-forward before-him, he-kissed the-ground between his-two-hands.
sentences.i: Then the vizier of Basra took Nūr al-Dīn with him and went up with him to the Sultan; and when he came forward into his presence, he kissed the ground before him.
sentences.n: ثُمَّ إِنَّ is a stock way of re-opening the story ("then indeed"); the إِنَّ need not be translated. بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, literally "between his two hands", means "in his presence".

sentences.t: وَكَانَ فَصِيحَ اللِّسَانِ ثَابِتَ الْجَنَانِ صَاحِبَ حُسْنٍ وَإِحْسَانٍ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna faṣīḥa al-lisāni thābita al-janāni ṣāḥiba ḥusnin wa-iḥsānin wa-anshada yaqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: And he-was eloquent-of the-tongue, firm-of the-heart, possessor-of goodness and-kindness; and he-recited, saying, poetry:
sentences.i: He was fluent of tongue and steadfast of heart, a man of grace and kindness; and he recited these verses:
sentences.n: فَصِيحَ, ثَابِتَ and صَاحِبَ are accusative because they complete كَانَ; each governs the genitive that follows ("eloquent of tongue"). الْجَنَان, "the heart", is a poetic word, and ثَابِتَ الْجَنَانِ means "unshaken".

sentences.t:
دَامَتْ لَكَ الْاِنْعَامُ يَاسَيِّدِي * وَدُمْتَ مَا دَامَ الدُّجَا وَالفَجْرُ
يَا مَنْ اِذَا مَا ذُكِرَتْ هِمَّتُهُ * رَقَصَ الزَّمَانُ وَصَفَّقَ الدَّهْرُ
sentences.tr:
dāmat laka al-in‘āmu yā sayyidī * wa-dumta mā dāma al-dujā wa-al-fajru
yā man idhā mā dhukirat himmatuhu * raqaṣa al-zamānu wa-ṣaffaqa al-dahru
sentences.l:
Lasted for-you the-favours, O my-master, * and you-lasted as-long-as lasted the-darkness and-the-dawn;
O one-who, when is-mentioned his-high-aim, * danced the-time and-clapped the-age.
sentences.i: May favours endure for you, my lord, and may you endure as long as darkness and dawn endure; O you whose high aim, when it is mentioned, makes Time dance and the Age clap its hands.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse and the pointing is kept as printed. دَامَتْ is a wish ("may [they] last"), not a statement; the feminine verb goes with الْاِنْعَامُ, which the poet treats as a plural of favours. The second line says that merely to name your high aim sets Time dancing.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ لَهُمَا السُّلْطَانُ وَشَكَرَ نُورَ الدِّينِ عَلَى مَا قَالَ وَقَالَ لِوَزِيرِهِ مَنْ هَذَا الشَّابُّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma lahumā al-sulṭānu wa-shakara Nūra al-Dīni ʿalā mā qāla wa-qāla li-wazīrihi man hādhā al-shābbu
sentences.l: So rose for-the-two-of-them the-Sultan, and thanked Nūr al-Dīn for what he-said, and said to-his-vizier: Who is-this the-youth?
sentences.i: The Sultan rose in honour of them both and thanked Nūr al-Dīn for what he had said, and he said to his vizier: Who is this young man?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ قِصَّتَهُ مِنْ أَوَّلِهَا إِلَى آخِرِهَا وَقَالَ لَهُ هَذَا ابْنُ أَخِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru qiṣṣatahu min awwalihā ilā ākhirihā wa-qāla lahu hādhā ibnu akhī
sentences.l: So said to-him the-vizier his-story from its-beginning to its-end, and said to-him: This is son-of my-brother.
sentences.i: Then the vizier told him the whole of the youth's story, from beginning to end, and said to him: This is my brother's son.
sentences.n: Here قَالَ takes the story itself as its object, so "said him his story" means "told him his story". The pronoun in أَوَّلِهَا refers back to the feminine قِصَّة.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَكَيْفَ يَكُونُ ابْنَ أَخِيكَ وَلَمْ نَسْمَعْ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu wa-kayfa yakūnu ibna akhīka wa-lam nasmaʿ bihi
sentences.l: So he-said to-him: And how can-he-be son-of your-brother, and we-have-not heard of-him?
sentences.i: He said to him: How can he be your brother's son, when we have never heard of him?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا مَوْلَانَا السُّلْطَانُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ لِي أَخٌ وَزِيرٌ بِالدِّيَارِ الْمِصْرِيَّةِ وَقَدْ مَاتَ وَخَلَّفَ وَلَدَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā mawlānā al-sulṭānu innahu kāna lī akhun wazīrun bi-al-diyāri al-Miṣriyyati wa-qad māta wa-khallafa waladayni
sentences.l: So he-said: O our-master the-Sultan, indeed-it [is that] there-was to-me a-brother, a-vizier in-the-lands the-Egyptian, and he-has-died and left two-sons.
sentences.i: He said: O our lord the Sultan, I had a brother, a vizier in the land of Egypt; he has died and left two sons.
sentences.n: إِنَّهُ كَانَ لِي is the "the fact is" use of إِنَّ with a pronoun that stands for the whole statement; it adds emphasis and is not translated. الدِّيَارِ الْمِصْرِيَّةِ, "the Egyptian lands", is the edition's usual way of saying Egypt.

sentences.t: فَالْكَبِيرُ جَلَسَ مَكَانَ وَالِدِهِ وَزِيرًا وَهَذَا وَلَدُهُ الصَّغِيرُ جَاءَ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-al-kabīru jalasa makāna wālidihi wazīran wa-hādhā waladuhu al-ṣaghīru jāʾa ʿindī
sentences.l: So the-elder sat in-place-of his-father as-vizier, and this his-son the-younger came at-me.
sentences.i: The elder has taken his father's place as vizier, and this is his younger son, who came to me.

sentences.t: وَحَلَفْتُ إِنِّي لَا أُزَوِّجُ بِنْتِي إِلَّا لَهُ فَلَمَّا جَاءَ زَوَّجْتُهُ بِهَا وَهُوَ شَابٌّ وَأَنَا بَقِيتُ شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا وَقَلَّ سَمْعِي وَعَجَزَ تَدْبِيرِي
sentences.tr: wa-ḥalaftu innī lā uzawwiju bintī illā lahu fa-lammā jāʾa zawwajtuhu bihā wa-huwa shābbun wa-anā baqītu shaykhan kabīran wa-qalla samʿī wa-ʿajaza tadbīrī
sentences.l: And I-swore that-I not I-marry-off my-daughter except to-him; and when he-came, I-married-him to-her, and he a-youth, and I remained an-old-man great-in-years, and diminished my-hearing, and failed my-management.
sentences.i: I had sworn that I would give my daughter in marriage to no one but him; and when he came, I married him to her, he being a young man while I had grown a very old man, my hearing failing and my judgement weakening.
sentences.n: The oath is reported as the speaker would have sworn it: حَلَفْتُ إِنِّي لَا أُزَوِّجُ, "I swore that I would not marry off". زَوَّجَهُ بِهَا, "married him to her", takes بِـ for the bride. تَدْبِير is management, hence good judgement.

sentences.t: وَالْقَصْدُ مِنْ مَوْلَانَا السُّلْطَانِ أَنْ يَجْعَلَهُ فِي مَرْتَبَتِي فَإِنَّهُ ابْنُ أَخِي وَزَوْجُ ابْنَتِي وَهُوَ أَهْلٌ لِلْوِزَارَةِ لِأَنَّهُ صَاحِبُ رَأْيٍ وَتَدْبِيرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-al-qaṣdu min mawlānā al-sulṭāni an yajʿalahu fī martabatī fa-innahu ibnu akhī wa-zawju ibnatī wa-huwa ahlun li-al-wizārati li-annahu ṣāḥibu raʾyin wa-tadbīrin
sentences.l: And the-aim from our-master the-Sultan [is] that he-make-him in my-rank; for indeed-he [is] son-of my-brother and husband-of my-daughter, and he [is] worthy for-the-vizierate, because-he [is] possessor-of opinion and-management.
sentences.i: What I ask of our lord the Sultan is that he set him in my rank; for he is my brother's son and my daughter's husband, and he is fit for the vizierate, being a man of sound counsel and good management.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ السُّلْطَانُ إِلَيْهِ فَلَاقَ بِخَاطِرِهِ فَأَنْعَمَ عَلَيْهِ بِمَا أَرَادَهُ الْوَزِيرُ وَقَدَّمَهُ فِى الْوِزَارَةِ وَأَسَرَّلَهُ بِخِلْعَةٍ عَظِيمَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara al-sulṭānu ilayhi fa-lāqa bi-khāṭirihi fa-anʿama ʿalayhi bi-mā arādahu al-wazīru wa-qaddamahu fī al-wizārati wa-asarralahu bi-khilʿatin ʿaẓīmatin
sentences.l: So looked the-Sultan at-him, and he-was-fitting to-his-mind; so he-bestowed-favour on-him with what wanted-it the-vizier, and advanced-him in the-vizierate, and [?asarra]-for-him with a-robe-of-honour great.
sentences.i: The Sultan looked at him and liked him, and granted him what the vizier desired, advanced him to the vizierate, and bestowed on him a splendid robe of honour.
sentences.n: لَاقَ بِخَاطِرِهِ means "it suited his mind", that is, he took to him. وَأَسَرَّلَهُ is obscure, and the edition may be corrupt here: the sense required is "and he bestowed on him", and the nearest candidates are أَسْبَغَ or أَسْبَلَ, "he lavished". I have pointed the letters as printed, as أَسَرَّ لَهُ, and I translate by the sense. The bestowal is introduced by بِـ, "with a robe of honour".

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ لَهُ السُّلْطَانُ بِبَغْلَةٍ مِنْ خَاصِّ مَرْكُوبِهِ وَعَيَّنَ لَهُ الرَّوَاتِبَ وَالْجَوَامِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-amara lahu al-sulṭānu bi-baghlatin min khāṣṣi markūbihi wa-ʿayyana lahu al-rawātiba wa-al-jawāmika
sentences.l: And ordered for-him the-Sultan a-mule from the-special-part-of his-mount, and appointed for-him the-stipends and the-salaries.
sentences.i: The Sultan also ordered a mule for him from his own private mounts, and fixed stipends and allowances for him.
sentences.n: أَمَرَ لَهُ بِـ is "ordered [that there be given] to him" something. الرَّوَاتِب (stipends, fixed pay) and الْجَوَامِك (cash salaries, a term of the Mamluk-period court) are the two kinds of regular pay.

sentences.t: فَقَبَّلَ نُورُالدِّينِ يَدَ السُّلْطَانِ وَنَزَلَ هُوَ وَصِهْرُهُ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِمَا وَهُمْ فِي غَايَةِ الْفَرَحِ وَقَالُوا هَذَا بِكَعْبِ الْمَوْلُودِ حَسَنٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qabbala Nūru al-Dīni yada al-sulṭāni wa-nazala huwa wa-ṣihruhu ilā manzilihimā wa-hum fī ghāyati al-faraḥi wa-qālū hādhā bi-kaʿbi al-mawlūdi Ḥasanin
sentences.l: So kissed Nūr al-Dīn the-hand-of the-Sultan, and descended he and-his-father-in-law to their-two's-house, and they in extremity-of the-joy; and they-said: This [is] by-the-heel-of the-newborn Ḥasan.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn kissed the Sultan's hand, and he and his father-in-law went down to their house in the utmost joy, saying: This is all thanks to the luck of the newborn Ḥasan.
sentences.n: Only two men go home, but the verbs and pronouns here (وَهُمْ, وَقَالُوا) are plural, presumably taking in their household; Middle Arabic is loose about such agreement. كَعْب is literally "heel" or "ankle"; بِكَعْبِ فُلَانٍ is, I take it, an idiom for "by the good luck of so-and-so", though I cannot confirm the sense from Lane.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ نُورَالدِّينِ تَوَجَّهَ ثَانِيَ يَوْمٍ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna Nūra al-Dīni tawajjaha thāniya yawmin ʿinda al-maliki wa-qabbala al-arḍa wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: Then indeed Nūr al-Dīn went, second-of day, at the-king, and kissed the-ground, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: Then, on the next day, Nūr al-Dīn went to the king, kissed the ground, and recited:
sentences.n: ثَانِيَ يَوْمٍ, "the second of a day", means "the next day". الْمَلِك, "the king", is the Sultan again.

sentences.t:
سَعَادَاتٌ تُجَدِّدُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ * وَاِنْبَانٌ عَلَى كَيْدِ الْحَسُودِ
فَمَا زَالَتْ لَكَ الْاَيَّامُ بِيْضٌ * وَاَيَّامُ الَّذِي عَادَاكَ سُودُ
sentences.tr:
suʿādātun tujaddidu kulla yawmin * wa-inbānun ʿalā kaydi al-ḥasūdi
fa-mā zālat laka al-ayyāmu bīḍun * wa-ayyāmu alladhī ʿādāka sūdu
sentences.l:
Felicities renewing every day, * and an-inbān against the-plotting-of the-envier;
so not ceased for-you the-days white, * and the-days-of him-who was-hostile-to-you black.
sentences.i: May happiness be renewed for you every day, and triumph over the schemes of the envious; may your days ever be white, and the days of your enemy black.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse and the pointing is kept as printed. اِنْبَانٌ is unclear to me and may be a misprint; I translate it "triumph" only on the guess that اِنْتِصَارٌ was meant. "White days" are happy days and "black" ones unhappy. بِيْضٌ is nominative as printed, though a classical predicate of زَالَ would be accusative. فَمَا زَالَتْ here is a prayer, "may they never cease".

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَهُ السُّلْطَانُ بِالْجُلُوسِ فِي مَرْتَبَةِ الْوِزَارَةِ فَجَلَسَ وَتَعَاطَى أُمُورَ خِدْمَتِهِ وَنَظَرَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ فِي أُمُورِهِمْ وَأَحْكَامِهِمْ كَمَا جَرَتْ عَادَةُ الْوُزَرَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-amarahu al-sulṭānu bi-al-julūsi fī martabati al-wizārati fa-jalasa wa-taʿāṭā umūra khidmatihi wa-naẓara bayna al-nāsi fī umūrihim wa-aḥkāmihim ka-mā jarat ʿādatu al-wuzarāʾi
sentences.l: So ordered-him the-Sultan to-the-sitting in the-rank-of the-vizierate; so he-sat, and undertook the-affairs-of his-service, and looked between the-people in their-affairs and-their-judgements, as ran the-custom-of the-viziers.
sentences.i: The Sultan commanded him to take his seat in the vizier's place, and he sat, and took in hand the business of his office, and gave judgement between the people in their affairs and their cases, as is the custom of viziers.
sentences.n: نَظَرَ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ, "looked between the people", means to judge their disputes. أَمَرَهُ بِـ is "commanded him to [do] something", and the thing commanded here is the sitting.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ السُّلْطَانُ يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِ وَيَتَعَجَّبُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ وَعَقْلِهِ وَتَدْبِيرِهِ وَتَصْرِيفِهِ فَحَبَّهُ وَقَرَّبَهُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra al-sulṭānu yanẓuru ilayhi wa-yataʿajjabu min amrihi wa-ʿaqlihi wa-tadbīrihi wa-taṣrīfihi fa-ḥabbahu wa-qarrabahu ilayhi
sentences.l: And became the-Sultan looking at-him and marvelling at his-affair and-his-intellect and-his-management and-his-conduct; so he-loved-him and drew-him-near to-him.
sentences.i: The Sultan took to watching him and marvelling at his bearing, his intellect, his judgement and his handling of affairs; and he came to love him and drew him close.
sentences.n: حَبَّهُ, "he loved him", is the simple verb; the classical verb for this is أَحَبَّهُ, but حَبَّ is also found. تَصْرِيف is the handling or management of affairs.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا انْصَرَفَ الدِّيوَانُ نَزَلَ نُورُالدِّينِ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَحَكَى لِصِهْرِهِ مَا وَقَعَ فَفَرِحَ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā inṣarafa al-dīwānu nazala Nūru al-Dīni ilā baytihi wa-ḥakā li-ṣihrihi mā waqaʿa fa-fariḥa
sentences.l: And when dispersed the-council, descended Nūr al-Dīn to his-house, and related to-his-father-in-law what happened; so he-rejoiced.
sentences.i: When the court rose, Nūr al-Dīn went down to his house and told his father-in-law what had happened, and the old man was glad.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ نُورُالدِّينِ فِى الْوِزَارَةِ حَتَّى إِنَّهُ لَا يُفَارِقُ السُّلْطَانَ لَافِي لَيْلٍ وَلَا فِي نَهَارٍ وَزَادَلَهُ الْجَوَامِكَ وَالْجَرَايَاتِ إِلَى أَنِ اتَّسَعَ لَهُ حَالٌ وَصَارَ لَهُ مَرَاكِبُ تُسَافِرُ مِنْ تَحْتِ يَدِهِ بِالْمَتَاجِرِ وَصَارَ لَهُ عَبِيدٌ وَمَمَالِيكُ وَعَمَّرَ أَمْلَاكًا كَثِيرَةً وَدَوَالِبَ وَبَسَاتِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal Nūru al-Dīni fī al-wizārati ḥattā innahu lā yufāriqu al-sulṭāna lā fī laylin wa-lā fī nahārin wa-zāda lahu al-jawāmika wa-al-jarāyāti ilā ani ittasaʿa lahu ḥālun wa-ṣāra lahu marākibu tusāfiru min taḥti yadihi bi-al-matājiri wa-ṣāra lahu ʿabīdun wa-mamālīku wa-ʿammara amlākan kathīratan wa-dawālība wa-basātīna
sentences.l: And he-did-not cease, Nūr al-Dīn, in the-vizierate, until indeed-he not leaves the-Sultan neither in night nor in day; and increased-for-him the-salaries and the-rations, until widened for-him a-condition; and there-became to-him ships travelling from under his-hand with-the-merchandise; and there-became to-him slaves and-mamluks; and he-built-up estates many, and waterwheels and gardens.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn remained in the vizierate until he could not part from the Sultan by night or by day; and the Sultan increased his salaries and rations until his fortunes grew broad. He came to own ships that sailed under his command with merchandise, and slaves and mamluks, and he built up many estates, water-wheels and gardens.
sentences.n: لَافِي is printed as one word, "not in", and I keep it joined. The subject of وَزَادَلَهُ is the Sultan, left unnamed. الْجَرَايَات (rations, allowances in kind) is the plural of جِرَايَة, a post-classical word. دَوَالِب, the plural of دُولَاب ("wheel"), here probably means water-wheels or mills. عَمَّرَ means "built up, developed".

sentences.t: وَصَارَ عُمْرُ وَلَدِهِ حَسَنٍ أَرْبَعَ سِنِينَ فَتُوُفِّيَ الْوَزِيرُ الْكَبِيرُ وَالزَّوْجَةُ نُورُالدِّينِ فَأَخْرَجَهُ خَرْجَةً عَظِيمَةً وَوَارَاهُ فِى التُّرَابِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra ʿumru waladihi Ḥasanin arbaʿa sinīna fa-tuwuffiya al-wazīru al-kabīru wa-al-zawjatu Nūru al-Dīni fa-akhrajahu kharjatan ʿaẓīmatan wa-wārāhu fī al-turābi
sentences.l: And became the-age-of his-son Ḥasan four years; so died the-vizier the-great and-the-wife Nūr al-Dīn; so he-brought-him-out a-procession great, and buried-him in the-dust.
sentences.i: When his son Ḥasan was four years old, the great vizier, his wife's father, died, and Nūr al-Dīn gave him a splendid funeral and laid him in the earth.
sentences.n: The words وَالزَّوْجَةُ نُورُالدِّينِ, "and the wife, Nūr al-Dīn", do not parse as printed. I read them as the remains of "the father of Nūr al-Dīn's wife", and the singular pronouns that follow show that only one man is buried. This is a guess. خَرْجَة is an outing or procession, here a funeral procession.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اشْتَغَلَ نُورُالدِّينِ بِتَرْبِيَةِ وَلَدِهِ فَلَمَّا اشْتَدَّ وَصَارَ لَهُ مِنَ الْعُمْرِ سَبْعُ سِنِينَ أَحْضَرَ لَهُ فَقِيهًا يُقْرِئُهُ فِي بَيْتِهِ وَأَوْصَاهُ بِتَعْلِيمِهِ وَأَدَبِهِ وَحُسْنِ تَرْبِيَتِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma ishtaghala Nūru al-Dīni bi-tarbiyati waladihi fa-lammā ishtadda wa-ṣāra lahu mina al-ʿumri sabʿu sinīna aḥḍara lahu faqīhan yuqriʾuhu fī baytihi wa-awṣāhu bi-taʿlīmihi wa-adabihi wa-ḥusni tarbiyatihi
sentences.l: Then busied-himself Nūr al-Dīn with-the-upbringing-of his-son; and when he-grew-strong, and there-became to-him of the-age seven years, he-brought for-him a-jurist who-makes-him-recite in his-house, and charged-him with-teaching-him and-his-manners and the-goodness-of his-upbringing.
sentences.i: Then Nūr al-Dīn busied himself with his son's upbringing; and when the boy had grown strong and was seven years old, he brought him a jurist to teach him to recite in his house, and charged the man with the boy's instruction, his manners, and the good ordering of his upbringing.
sentences.n: يُقْرِئُهُ, "makes him recite", is the teacher's work of drilling the Qurʾān. أَوْصَاهُ بِـ is "charged him with", so the jurist is the one charged.

sentences.t: فَقَرَأَهُ وَحَفِظَهُ فَوَائِدَ فِى الْعِلْمِ وَعَادَالْقُرْآنَ فِي مُدَّةِ سَنَوَاتٍ وَمَا زَالَ حَسَنٌ يَزْدَادُ جَمَالًا وَقَدًّا وَاعْتِدَالًا
sentences.tr: fa-qaraʾahu wa-ḥafiẓahu fawāʾida fī al-ʿilmi wa-ʿāda al-Qurʾāna fī muddati sanawātin wa-mā zāla Ḥasanun yazdādu jamālan wa-qaddan wa-iʿtidālan
sentences.l: So he-read-it and-memorised-it, benefits in the-knowledge, and returned-to the-Qurʾān in a-period-of years; and not ceased Ḥasan increasing in-beauty and-stature and-symmetry.
sentences.i: So he read it and learned it by heart, with useful points of learning, and went over the Qurʾān again within a few years; and Ḥasan grew ever more beautiful in his looks, his stature and his symmetry.
sentences.n: This sentence is tangled in print. As printed, the verbs have a single subject with the boy and the Qurʾān as objects, and فَوَائِدَ فِى الْعِلْمِ is left hanging, "benefits in learning". It may be that causatives were meant (فَأَقْرَأَهُ, "he made him read it", with the jurist as subject), and that وَعَادَالْقُرْآنَ stands for وَأَعَادَ الْقُرْآنَ, "and repeated the Qurʾān". The edition prints it as one word, and I translate by the general sense.

sentences.t: كَا قِيلَ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: kā qīla shiʿrun
sentences.l: As it-was-said, poetry:
sentences.i: As the poet says:
sentences.n: كَا is a short spelling for كَمَا, "as". شِعْر is the word "poetry", with the verses that follow.

sentences.t:
قَمَرٌ تَكَامَلَ فِي سَمَاءِ جَمَالِهِ * وَالشَّمْسُ تُشْرِقُ مِنْ شَقَائِقِ خَدِّهِ
مَلَكَ الْجَمَالَ بِاَسْرِهِ فَكَاَنَّمَا * حُسْنُ الْبَرِيَّةِ كُلُّهَا مِنْ عِنْدِهِ
sentences.tr:
qamarun takāmala fī samāʾi jamālihi * wa-al-shamsu tushriqu min shaqāʾiqi khaddihi
malaka al-jamāla bi-asrihi fa-ka-annamā * ḥusnu al-bariyyati kulluhā min ʿindihi
sentences.l:
A-moon perfected in the-sky-of his-beauty, * and the-sun rises from the-anemones-of his-cheek;
he-possessed the-beauty in-its-entirety, so-as-though * the-loveliness-of the-creation, all-of-it, [is] from with-him.
sentences.i: A moon grown full in the sky of his beauty, while the sun rises from the anemones of his cheek; he has taken all beauty whole, as though the loveliness of all creation came from him.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse and the pointing is kept as printed. شَقَائِق (anemones, red poppies) is a stock image for red cheeks, so the sun rising from them is a blush. بِاَسْرِهِ, literally "with its capture", means "in its entirety".

sentences.t: وَقَدْ رَبَّاهُ الْفَقِيهُ فِي قَصْرِأَبِيهِ وَمِنْ حِينَ نَشَأَ لَمْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ قَصْرِالْوِزَارَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad rabbāhu al-faqīhu fī qaṣri abīhi wa-min ḥīni nashaʾa lam yakhruj min qaṣri al-wizārati
sentences.l: And indeed raised-him the jurist in the-palace-of-his-father; and from the-time he-grew-up not he-went-out from the-palace-of-the-vizierate.
sentences.i: The tutor had brought him up in his father's palace, and from the time he grew up he had never gone out from the vizier's palace.
sentences.n: قَصْرِأَبِيهِ and قَصْرِالْوِزَارَةِ are printed as one word each, the second noun run on to the first ("palace-of-his-father", "palace-of-the-vizierate"). Such run-together annexations are a habit of this edition; the glossary splits them. الْفَقِيهُ is the boy's tutor, a man learned in religious law.

sentences.t: فَفِي يَوْمٍ مِنْ بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ أَخَذَهُ وَالِدُهُ الْوَزِيرُ نُورُالدِّينِ وَأَلْبَسَهُ بَدْلَةً مِنْ أَفْخَرِ مَلْبُوسِهِ وَرَكَّبَهُ بَغْلَةً مِنْ خِيَارِ بِغَالِهِ وَطَلَعَ بِهِ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ وَدَخَلَ بِهِ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-fī yawmin min baʿḍi al-ayyāmi akhadhahu wālduhu al-wazīru Nūru al-Dīni wa-albasahu badlatan min afkhari malbūsihi wa-rakkabahu baghlatan min khiyāri bighālihi wa-ṭalaʿa bihi ilā al-sulṭāni wa-dakhala bihi ʿalayhi
sentences.l: So on a-day from some-of the-days, took-him his-father the-vizier Nūr al-Dīn, and-clothed-him a-suit from the-most-splendid-of his-clothing, and-mounted-him a-mule from the-choice-of his-mules, and-went-up with-him to the-Sultan, and-entered with-him upon-him.
sentences.i: So one day his father the vizier Nūr al-Dīn took him, clothed him in a suit of the finest of his garments, mounted him on a mule of the best of his mules, and went up with him to the Sultan and brought him in before him.
sentences.n: مِنْ بَعْضِ الْأَيَّامِ ("from some of the days") is a stock way of saying "one day".

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ الْمَلِكُ بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ ابْنَ الْوَزِيرِ نُورِالدِّينِ فَأَعْجَبَهُ وَحَبَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara al-maliku Badra al-Dīni Ḥasana ibna al-wazīri Nūri al-Dīni fa-aʿjabahu wa-ḥabbahu
sentences.l: Then looked the-king at Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, son-of the-vizier Nūr al-Dīn, and-he-pleased-him and-he-loved-him.
sentences.i: Then the king looked at Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, the son of the vizier Nūr al-Dīn, and was pleased with him and loved him.
sentences.n: Here نَظَرَ takes its object directly; Classical Arabic would normally say نَظَرَ إِلَى. Throughout this passage "the king" and "the Sultan" are the same man.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا أَهْلُ الْمَمْلَكَةِ لَمَّا مَرَّ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَهُوَ طَالِعٌ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ فَانْبَهَتُوا مِنْ حُسْنِهِ وَجَلَسُوا فِي طَرِيقِهِ يَنْتَظِرُونَ عَوْدَةً عَلَيْهِمْ لِيَتَفَرَّجُوا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى حُسْنِهِ وَجَمَالِهِ وَقَدِّهِ وَاعْتِدَالِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā ahlu al-mamlakati lammā marra ʿalayhim awwala marratin wa-huwa ṭāliʿun maʿa abīhi ilā al-maliki fa-nbahatū min ḥusnihi wa-jalasū fī ṭarīqihi yantaẓirūna ʿawdatan ʿalayhim li-yatafarrajū ʿalayhi wa-ʿalā ḥusnihi wa-jamālihi wa-qaddihi wa-iʿtidālihi
sentences.l: And as-for the-people-of the-kingdom, when he-passed upon-them the-first time, while-he going-up with his-father to the-king, they-were-struck-dumb at his-beauty, and-sat in his-road, awaiting a-return upon-them, so-that-they-might-gaze upon-him and upon his-beauty and-his-loveliness and-his-stature and-his-evenness-of-form.
sentences.i: As for the people of the kingdom, when he passed among them the first time, going up with his father to the king, they were struck dumb by his beauty. They sat down along his road, waiting for him to come back past them, so that they might gaze at him, at his beauty and loveliness, his stature and the symmetry of his form.
sentences.n: فَانْبَهَتُوا is the seventh verb-form ("they were stunned"), made from بَهَتَ; Classical usage would more usually be the passive بُهِتُوا. It is a Middle Arabic form. عَوْدَةً عَلَيْهِمْ is printed without a pronoun ("a return upon them"); the sense is "his coming back to them". لِيَتَفَرَّجُوا, "that they might gaze", is a later, post-Classical verb for looking at a spectacle for pleasure.

sentences.t: كَمَا قِيلَ فِيهِ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتُ شِعْرٌ
sentences.tr: kamā qīla fīhi hādhihi al-abyātu shiʿrun
sentences.l: As was-said about-him these the-verses: poetry.
sentences.i: As these verses were said of him:

sentences.t:
رَصَدَ الْمُنَجِّمُ لَيْلَةً فَبَدَا لَهُ * قَدُّ الْمَلِيحِ يَتِيهُ فِي بُرْدَيْهِ
وَتَاَمَّلَ الْجَوْزَاءُ اِذْ نَشَرَتْ لَهُ * حُسْنَ الْجَمَالِ يَلُوحُ مِنْ عِطْفَيْهِ
وَاَتَى لَهُ زُحَلُ السَّوَادَ بِشَعْرِهِ * وَحَبَاهُ لَوْنَ الْمِسْكِ فِي صُدْغَيْهِ
اَهْدَى لَهُ الْمِرِّيخُ حُمْرَةَ خَدِّهِ * وَالْقَوْسُ يَرْمِي النَّبْلَ مِنْ جَفْنَيْهِ
وَعُطَارِدٌ اَعْطَاهُ فَرْطَ ذَكَائِهِ * وَاَبَا السُّهَا نَظَرَ الْوُشَاةِ اِلَيْهِ
فَبَقِي الْمُنَجِّمُ حَائِراً مِمَّارَاَى * وَسَعَى وَبَاسَ الاَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr:
raṣada al-munajjimu laylatan fa-badā lahu * qaddu al-malīḥi yatīhu fī burdayhi
wa-taʾammala al-jawzāʾu idh nasharat lahu * ḥusna al-jamāli yalūḥu min ʿiṭfayhi
wa-atā lahu zuḥalu al-sawāda bi-shaʿrihi * wa-ḥabāhu lawna al-miski fī ṣudghayhi
ahdā lahu al-mirrīkhu ḥumrata khaddihi * wa-al-qawsu yarmī al-nabla min jafnayhi
wa-ʿuṭāridun aʿṭāhu farṭa dhakāʾihi * wa-abā al-suhā naẓara al-wushāti ilayhi
fa-baqiya al-munajjimu ḥāʾiran mimmā raʾā * wa-saʿā wa-bāsa al-arḍa bayna yadayhi
sentences.i: An astrologer kept watch one night, and there appeared to him the stature of the handsome youth, strutting in his two mantles. Gemini pondered, when it unfolded for him the beauty of loveliness shining from his two sides. Saturn brought him the blackness for his hair and granted him the colour of musk upon his temples; Mars gave him the redness of his cheek, and Sagittarius shoots arrows from his eyelids. Mercury gave him an excess of his own quick wit, and Abā al-Suhā gave him the gaze of the slanderers fixed upon him. So the astrologer remained bewildered at what he saw, and hurried forward and kissed the ground before him.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse and the pointing is kept as printed, including the hamzas it leaves unwritten (تَاَمَّلَ, اَتَى). The poem says that each planet endowed the boy with a gift: Saturn (زُحَلُ) his black hair, Mars (الْمِرِّيخُ) the red of his cheek, Mercury (عُطَارِدٌ) his keen wits, and Sagittarius (الْقَوْسُ, the bow) his arrow-glancing eyelids. مِمَّارَاَى is مِمَّا رَأَى ("at what he saw") run together. The fifth line is obscure: أَبَا السُّهَا is probably the faint star Alcor, used as a test of eyesight, but how it governs نَظَرَ الْوُشَاةِ is uncertain, and the translation follows the words as printed. The lines rhyme on -ayhi.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَآهُ السُّلْطَانُ أَنْعَمَ عَلَيْهِ وَحَبَّهُ وَقَلٰ لِأَبِيهِ يَا وَزِيرُ لَازِمٌ وَلَا بُدَّ أَنَّكَ دَائِمًا يُحْضِرُهُ مَعَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhu al-sulṭānu anʿama ʿalayhi wa-ḥabbahu wa-qāla li-abīhi yā wazīru lāzimun wa-lā budda annaka dāʾiman yuḥḍiruhu maʿaka
sentences.l: So when saw-him the-Sultan, he-bestowed-favour upon-him and-loved-him, and-said to-his-father: O vizier, necessary and-no escape that-you always he-brings-him with-you.
sentences.i: When the Sultan saw him, he showed him favour and loved him, and said to his father: Vizier, you must, without fail, always bring him with you.
sentences.n: قَلٰ is the edition's defective spelling of قَالَ, pointed here with a dagger alif. يُحْضِرُهُ is third person after أَنَّكَ ("you"); the sense requires "you bring him" (تُحْضِرُهُ), so this is either a Middle Arabic lapse or a misprint, and the translation reads it as "you bring". لَازِمٌ وَلَا بُدَّ means "it is necessary, and there is no way round it".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ السَّمْعُ وَالطَّاعَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-samʿu wa-al-ṭāʿatu
sentences.l: So he-said: Hearing and-obedience.
sentences.i: So he said: With hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: This is the courtly formula of assent, with the rest of the phrase left out; it is not a sentence with a verb.

sentences.t: وَعَادَ الْوَزِيرُ بِوَلَدِهِ إِلَى مَنْزِلِهِ وَمَازَالَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ يَطْلُعُ بِهِ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ إِلَى أَنْ بَلَغَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْعُمْرِ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً
sentences.tr: wa-ʿāda al-wazīru bi-waladihi ilā manzilihi wa-māzāla kulla yawmin yaṭluʿu bihi ilā al-sulṭāni ilā an balagha al-waladu mina al-ʿumri khamsata ʿashara sanatan
sentences.l: And returned the-vizier with-his-son to his-house, and-he-did-not-cease every day he-goes-up with-him to the-Sultan, until reached the-boy from the-age fifteen year.
sentences.i: The vizier went back to his house with his son, and every day thereafter he went up with him to the Sultan, until the boy reached the age of fifteen.
sentences.n: خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً pairs a masculine number with a feminine noun, where Classical Arabic would write خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً; the form is kept as printed. مَازَالَ ("he did not cease") is printed as one word and, with the verb that follows it, means "he kept on doing".

sentences.t: فَضَعُفَ وَالِدُهُ نُورُالدِّينِ الْوَزِيرُ فَأَحْضَرَ وَلَدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaʿufa wālduhu Nūru al-Dīni al-wazīru fa-aḥḍara waladahu
sentences.l: Then grew-weak his-father Nūr al-Dīn the-vizier, and-he-summoned his-son.
sentences.i: Then his father, the vizier Nūr al-Dīn, grew weak, and he summoned his son.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ يَا وَلَدِي اعْلَمْ أَنَّ الدُّنْيَا دَارُ فَنَاءٍ وَالْآخِرَةَ دَارُ بَقَاءٍ وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أُوصِيَكَ بَعْضَ وَصَايَا فَافْهَمْ مَا أَقُولُ لَكَ وَأَصْغِ ذِهْنَكَ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla yā waladī iʿlam anna al-dunyā dāru fanāʾin wa-al-ākhirata dāru baqāʾin wa-urīdu an ūṣiyaka baʿḍa waṣāyā fa-ifham mā aqūlu laka wa-aṣghi dhihnaka ilayhi
sentences.l: And he-said: O my-son, know that the-world is house-of passing-away and-the-hereafter house-of remaining, and-I-want that I-charge-you some charges; so-understand what I-say to-you and-incline your-mind to-it.
sentences.i: And he said: My son, know that this world is a house of passing and the hereafter a house of lasting. I wish to give you some counsels, so understand what I say to you and lend it your full attention.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ يُوصِيهِ عَلَى حُسْنِ عِشْرَةِ النَّاسِ وَالتَّدْبِيرِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra yūṣīhi ʿalā ḥusni ʿishrati al-nāsi wa-al-tadbīri
sentences.l: And he-became charging-him upon good-companionship-of the-people and-the-management.
sentences.i: And he went on to counsel him on keeping good company with people and on managing his affairs wisely.
sentences.n: يُوصِيهِ عَلَى ("charges him upon") uses عَلَى where Classical Arabic has بِـ after أَوْصَى; it is a Middle Arabic habit. التَّدْبِيرِ is the prudent ordering of one's affairs.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ نُورَالدِّينِ تَذَكَّرَ أَخَاهُ وَأَوْطَانَهُ وَبِلَادَهُ فَبَكَى عَلَى فُرْقَةِ الْأَحْبَابِ وَمَسَحَ دُمُوعَهُ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: thumma inna Nūra al-Dīni tadhakkara akhāhu wa-awṭānahu wa-bilādahu fa-bakā ʿalā furqati al-aḥbābi wa-masaḥa dumūʿahu wa-anshada yaqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: Then indeed Nūr al-Dīn remembered his-brother and-his-homelands and-his-lands, and-wept over the-separation-from the-loved-ones, and-wiped his-tears, and-recited, saying, poetry.
sentences.i: Then Nūr al-Dīn remembered his brother, his homeland and his native cities, and he wept over the parting from his loved ones, wiped away his tears, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: The brother is Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad, whom he had left in Egypt. أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ is a pairing of two verbs, "he recited, saying".

sentences.t:
اِنْ شَكَوْنَا بُعْدًا فَمَا ذَا نَقُولُ * اَوْ بَلَغْنَا شَوْقًا فَكَيْفَ السَّبِيلُ
اَوْ بَعَثْنَا رَسُولًا يُتَرْجِمُ عَنَّا * مَايُؤَدِّي شَكْوَى اَثْبَتَ رَسُولُ
اَوْ صَبَرْنَا فَمَا بَقِي مُحِبٌّ * بَعْدَ فَقْدِ الْاَحْبَابِ اِلَّا قَلِيلُ
لَيْسَ الْآنَ اِلَّا تَاَسُّفًا وَحَنِينًا * وَدُمُوعًا عَلَى الْخَدِّ تَسِيلُ
اَيَا غَائِبِينَ عَنْ شَخْصِ عَيْنِي * وَطَرْفِي وَهُمْ فِي فُؤَادِي حُلُولُ
اَتَرَاكُمْ اَنْتُمُ اَنَّ عَهْدِي * عَلَى طُولِ الصُّدُودِ لَا يَحُولُ
اَمْ تَنَاسَيْتُمْ عَلَى الْبُعْدِ صَبًّا * شَفَى فِيكُمُ الْبُكَاءُ وَالنُّحُولُ
اِنَّا وَاِنْ ضَمَّنَا وَاِيَّاكُمُ الْحَيُّ * لِيْ مَعَكُمْ هُنَاكَ عِتَابٌ يَطُولُ
sentences.tr:
in shakawnā buʿdan fa-mā dhā naqūlu * aw balaghnā shawqan fa-kayfa al-sabīlu
aw baʿathnā rasūlan yutarjimu ʿannā * mā yuʾaddī shakwā athbata rasūlu
aw ṣabarnā fa-mā baqiya muḥibbun * baʿda faqdi al-aḥbābi illā qalīlu
laysa al-āna illā taʾassufan wa-ḥanīnan * wa-dumūʿan ʿalā al-khaddi tasīlu
ayā ghāʾibīna ʿan shakhṣi ʿaynī * wa-ṭarfī wa-hum fī fuʾādī ḥulūlu
a-tarākum antumu anna ʿahdī * ʿalā ṭūli al-ṣudūdi lā yaḥūlu
am tanāsaytum ʿalā al-buʿdi ṣabban * shafā fīkumu al-bukāʾu wa-al-nuḥūlu
innā wa-in ḍammanā wa-iyyākumu al-ḥayyu * lī maʿakum hunāka ʿitābun yaṭūlu
sentences.l:
If we-complain of-distance, then what shall-we-say? * Or we-reached longing, then how the-way?
Or we-sent a-messenger he-interprets for-us * what he-conveys a-complaint — has-proved a-messenger?
Or we-were-patient, yet-not remained a-lover * after the-loss-of the-loved-ones except a-few.
There-is-not now except lamenting and-yearning * and-tears upon the-cheek flowing.
O absent-ones from the-person-of my-eye * and-my-glance, while-they in my-heart dwelling,
do-you-suppose, you, that my-covenant * over the-length-of the-estrangement does-not change?
Or have-you-feigned-forgetfulness, despite the-distance, of-a-lover * whom-has-brought-to-the-brink for-you the-weeping and-the-emaciation?
Indeed-we, even-if the-tribe-encampment gathers-us and-you, * I-have with-you there a-reproach that-lasts-long.
sentences.i: If we complain of the distance, what shall we say? Or if longing overtakes us, how then is the way? Or if we send a messenger to speak for us, what would convey a complaint — has any messenger proved able? Or if we are patient, still no lover remains, after the loss of the beloved, except a few. There is nothing now but lamenting and yearning and tears running down the cheek. O you who are absent from the sight of my eye and my glance, while you dwell in my heart: do you suppose that my pledge, through the long estrangement, will ever change? Or have you, across the distance, forgotten a lover whom weeping and wasting for your sake have brought to the brink? Even if the encampment gathers us and you together, I have a reproach against you there that will run long.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse, and the pointing is kept as printed. Three places are uncertain. In line 1, بَلَغْنَا شَوْقًا is read as "we reached the point of longing" or "longing reached us". In line 2, the meaning of مَايُؤَدِّي شَكْوَى اَثْبَتَ رَسُولُ is difficult and the translation is a best guess: no messenger could prove able to carry the complaint. In line 7, شَفَى is read as "brought to the brink" (the sense of شَفَا, "edge"); the other possible reading, "healed", would make the line ironic. The poem is Nūr al-Dīn's lament for his brother Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad and his lost home. It rhymes on -ūlu throughout.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ إِنْشَادِهِ وَبُكَائِهِ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى وَلَدِهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min inshādihi wa-bukāʾihi iltafata ilā waladihi wa-qāla lahu
sentences.l: So when he-finished from his-reciting and-his-weeping, he-turned to his-son and-said to-him:
sentences.i: When he had finished his recitation and his weeping, he turned to his son and said to him:

sentences.t: اعْلَمْ قَبْلَ مَا أُوصِيكَ أَنَّ لَكَ عَمٌّ وَهُوَ وَزِيرٌ بِمِصْرَ فَارَقْتُهُ وَخَرَجْتُ عَلَى غَيْرِ رِضَاهُ
sentences.tr: iʿlam qabla mā ūṣīka anna laka ʿammun wa-huwa wazīrun bi-Miṣra fāraqtuhu wa-kharajtu ʿalā ghayri riḍāhu
sentences.l: Know, before what I-charge-you, that to-you an-uncle, and-he a-vizier in-Egypt; I-parted-from-him and-I-went-out upon other-than his-satisfaction.
sentences.i: Know, before I give you my charge, that you have an uncle who is a vizier in Egypt. I parted from him and left without his blessing.
sentences.n: عَمٌّ is printed without any mark and stands where classical grammar would put the accusative عَمًّا after أَنَّ. It is vocalised as the print has it, a Middle Arabic feature to note and move past. The speaker means Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad, his brother.

sentences.t: وَالْقَصْدُ أَنَّكَ تَأْخُذُ دَرْجًا وَتَكْتُبُ فِيهِ مَا أَقُولُ لَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-qaṣdu annaka taʾkhudhu darjan wa-taktubu fīhi mā aqūlu laka
sentences.l: And-the-aim, that-you you-take a-scroll and-you-write in-it what I-say to-you.
sentences.i: What I want is that you take a scroll and write down in it what I tell you.

sentences.t: فَأخَذَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ دَرْجًا مِنَ الْوَرَقِ وَصَارَ يَكْتُبُ فِيهِ كَمَا قَالَ أَبُوهُ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan darjan mina al-waraqi wa-ṣāra yaktubu fīhi kamā qāla abūhu
sentences.l: So took Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan a-scroll of the-paper, and-became writing in-it as said his-father.
sentences.i: So Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan took a scroll of paper and began to write in it just as his father spoke.

sentences.t: فَأمْلَأَهُ مَاجَرَى لَهُ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-amlaʾahu mājarā lahu mina al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri
sentences.l: So he-filled-it with-what happened to-him, from the-first to the-last.
sentences.i: So he filled it with all that had befallen him, from beginning to end.
sentences.n: فَا^مْلَأَهُ is printed with a hamza on the last-but-one letter and none after the alif, an odd spelling. It is probably for فَمَلَأَهُ, "and he filled it", though فَأَمْلَاهُ, "and he dictated it to him", would also suit the scene. It is vocalised here as the first, which is the nearest to the printed letters.

sentences.t: وَكَتَبَ لَهُ تَارِيخَ زَوَاجِهِ وَدُخُولِهِ عَلَى بِنْتِ الْوَزِيرِ وَتَارِيخَ وُصُولِهِ إِلَى الْبَصْرَةِ وَاجْتِمَاعِهِ بِوَزِيرِهِ وَأَنَّ عُمْرَهُ دُونَ الْأَرْبَعِينَ مِنْ يَوْمِ النِّزَاعِ
sentences.tr: wa-kataba lahu tārīkha zawājihi wa-dukhūlihi ʿalā bint al-wazīri wa-tārīkha wuṣūlihi ilā al-Baṣrati wa-ijtimāʿihi bi-wazīrihi wa-anna ʿumrahu dūna al-arbaʿīna min yawmi al-nizāʿi
sentences.l: And-he-wrote for-him the-date of-his-marriage and-his-entering upon the-daughter of-the-vizier, and-the-date of-his-arrival at al-Basra and-his-meeting with-his-vizier, and-that his-age less-than the-forty from the-day of-the-dispute.
sentences.i: He wrote down for him the date of his marriage and of his going in to the vizier's daughter, the date of his arrival at Basra and of his meeting with his vizier, and that his age was under forty, counted from the day of the quarrel.
sentences.n: The Arabic does not say whose age is meant or what the quarrel was, so the literal layer keeps it as printed. "Going in to" is the Nights' frank idiom for the wedding night. Note the doubled pair تَارِيخَ ... وَتَارِيخَ, "the date of ... and the date of".

sentences.t: وَهَذَا كِتَابِي إِلَيْهِ وَاللَّهُ خَلِيفَتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā kitābī ilayhi wa-Allāhu khalīfatī min baʿdi dhālika ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-this my-letter to-him, and-God my-successor from after that over-him.
sentences.i: This is my letter to him, and after this God stands in my place over him.
sentences.n: This is part of what Nūr al-Dīn has the boy write down: the note ends with a prayer committing the son to God's guardianship.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَوَاهَا وَخَتَمَهَا وَقَالَ يَا وَلَدِي حَسَنُ احْفَظِ الْوَصِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭawāhā wa-khatamahā wa-qāla yā waladī Ḥasanu iḥfaẓi al-waṣiyyata
sentences.l: Then he-folded-it and-sealed-it and-said: O my-son Ḥasan, guard the-testament,
sentences.i: Then he folded it and sealed it, and said: My son Ḥasan, keep this charge,

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ الرُّقْعَةَ فِيهَا أَصْلُكَ وَحَسَبُكَ وَنَسَبُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-inna al-ruqʿata fīhā aṣluka wa-ḥasabuka wa-nasabuka
sentences.l: for indeed the-note in-it your-origin and-your-merit and-your-lineage.
sentences.i: for in this note are your origin, your standing and your lineage.
sentences.n: حَسَب is the standing one inherits through one's forebears' deeds, نَسَب is the line of descent itself; the two often come as a rhyming pair.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ أَصَابَكَ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الْأُمُورِ فَاعْمِدْ إِلَى مِصْرَ وَاسْأَلْ عَلَى عَمِّكَ وَاسْتَدِلَّ عَلَيْهِ وَأَعْلِمْهُ أَنِّي مُتُّ غَرِيبًا مُشْتَاقًا
sentences.tr: fa-in aṣābaka shayʾun mina al-umūri fa-iʿmid ilā Miṣra wa-isʾal ʿalā ʿammika wa-istadilla ʿalayhi wa-aʿlimhu annī muttu gharīban mushtāqan
sentences.l: So-if befalls-you something of the-affairs, then make-for Egypt and-ask upon your-uncle and-seek-guidance upon-him, and-inform-him that-I died a-stranger, longing.
sentences.i: If anything of life's troubles befalls you, make for Egypt, ask after your uncle, find your way to him, and tell him that I died far from home, full of longing.
sentences.n: عَلَى after سَأَلَ, "ask about", and عَلَى after اسْتَدَلَّ, "be guided to", are non-classical uses of the preposition, easy to follow in context.

sentences.t: فَأخَذَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ الرُّقْعَةَ وَطَوَاهَا وَخَيَّطَهَا بَيْنَ الْبِطَانَةِ وَالظِّهَارَةِ وَلَفَّ عَلَيْهَا شَاشَهُ وَهُوَ يَبْكِي عَلَى أَبِيهِ وَعَلَى فِرَاقِهِ وَهُوَ صَغِيرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan al-ruqʿata wa-ṭawāhā wa-khayyaṭahā bayna al-biṭānati wa-al-ẓihārati wa-laffa ʿalayhā shāshahu wa-huwa yabkī ʿalā abīhi wa-ʿalā firāqihi wa-huwa ṣaghīrun
sentences.l: So took Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan the-note and-folded-it and-sewed-it between the-lining and-the-outer-cloth, and-wound over-it his-turban-cloth, while-he weeping over his-father and-over parting-from-him, and-he small.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan took the note, folded it, and sewed it between the lining and the outer cloth; then he wound his turban over it, weeping for his father and for their parting, young as he was.
sentences.n: The print does not name the garment, but the lining and outer cloth must be those of his cap, with the turban wound on top. شَاشَهُ is read as "his turban-cloth" (the final ه for ة is not certain; it could also be شَاشَةً, "a turban-cloth").

sentences.t: وَقَالَ نُورُالدِّينِ إِنِّي أُوصِيكَ بِخَمْسَةِ وَصَايَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla Nūr al-Dīn innī ūṣīka bi-khamsati waṣāyā
sentences.l: And-said Nūr al-Dīn: Indeed-I I-charge-you with-five charges.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said: I charge you with five counsels.

sentences.t: آوَّلُهَا أَنْ لَاتُعَاشِرَ أَحَدًا تَسْلَمْ مِنْ شَرِّهِ فَإِنَّ السَّلَامَةَ فِى الْعُزْلَةِ وَلَا تُخَالِطَهُ وَلَا تُبَاشِرَهُ
sentences.tr: awwaluhā an lā tuʿāshira aḥadan taslam min sharrihi fa-inna al-salāmata fī al-ʿuzlati wa-lā tukhāliṭahu wa-lā tubāshirahu
sentences.l: The-first-of-them: that not you-associate-with anyone, you-are-safe from his-evil; for indeed the-safety is in the-seclusion; and-not you-mingle-with-him and-not you-have-dealings-with-him.
sentences.i: The first is that you keep company with no one, and so be safe from his evil; for safety lies in solitude. Do not mingle with anyone, nor have close dealings with him.
sentences.n: لَاتُعَاشِرَ is printed as one word. The jussive تَسْلَمْ answers the command like "and you will be safe". Note that the print writes فِى with ى for فِي.

sentences.t: فَإِنِّي سَمِعْتُ الشَّاعِرَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-innī samiʿtu al-shāʿira yaqūlu
sentences.l: For-indeed-I I-heard the-poet saying:
sentences.i: For I have heard the poet say:

sentences.t:
مَافِي زَمَانِكَ مَنْ تَرْجُو مَوَدَّتُهُ * وَلَا صَدِيقٌ اِذَا جَارَ الزَّمَانُ وَفِى
فَعِشْ فَرِيدًا وَلَا تَرْكَنْ اِلَى اَحَدٍ * فَقَدْ نَصَحْتُكَ فِيمَا قُلْتُهُ وَكَفَى
sentences.tr:
mā fī zamānika man tarjū mawaddatahu * wa-lā ṣadīqun idhā jāra al-zamānu wafā
fa-ʿish farīdan wa-lā tarkan ilā aḥadin * fa-qad naṣaḥtuka fīmā qultuhu wa-kafā
sentences.l:
Not in your-time one-whom you-hope for his-affection, * and-not a-friend, when the-time wrongs, who-kept-faith;
so live solitary, and-not you-lean to anyone, * for I-have-advised-you in-what I-said, and-sufficed.
sentences.i: In your time there is no one whose affection you can hope for, nor any friend who keeps faith when the times turn unjust. So live alone, and lean on no one; I have given you my counsel, and that is enough.
sentences.n: The poem's rhyme falls on -fā: وَفِى (printed with a kasra under the ى, kept as printed) is the verb "he kept faith", wafā, and the second line ends كَفَى, kafā.

sentences.t: آلثَّانِيَةُ يَا وَلَدِي لَاتَجُورْ عَلَى أَحَدٍ يَجُورْ عَلَيْكَ الدَّهْرُ فَالدَّهْرُ يَوْمٌ لَكَ وَيَوْمٌ عَلَيْكَ
sentences.tr: al-thāniyatu yā waladī lā tajūr ʿalā aḥadin yajūr ʿalayka al-dahru fa-al-dahru yawmun laka wa-yawmun ʿalayka
sentences.l: The-second: O my-son, not you-wrong against anyone, wrongs against-you the-age; for the-age a-day for-you and-a-day against-you.
sentences.i: The second: my son, do not wrong anyone, or Time will wrong you; for Time is one day for you and one day against you.
sentences.n: The print keeps the long ū in تَجُورْ and يَجُورْ, where the classical jussive would shorten it (تَجُرْ). This is vocalised as printed. الدَّهْر is Time as fate, the force that turns fortune.

sentences.t: الدُّنْيَا قَرْضٌ بِوَفَاءٍ
sentences.tr: al-dunyā qarḍun bi-wafāʾin
sentences.l: The-world a-loan with-repayment.
sentences.i: This world is a loan, and it is repaid in full.

sentences.t: وَلَقَدْ سَمِعْتُ الشَّاعِرَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-la-qad samiʿtu al-shāʿira yaqūlu
sentences.l: And-indeed I-heard the-poet saying:
sentences.i: And I have indeed heard the poet say:

sentences.t:
تَانَّ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ لِاَمْرٍ تُرِيدُهُ * وَكُنْ رَاحِمًا لِلنَّاسِ تُدْعَى بِرَاحِمِ
فَمَا مِنْ يَدٍ اِلَّا يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَهَا * وَلَا ظَالِمٍ اِلَّا سَيُبْلَى بِظَالِمِ
sentences.tr:
tānna wa-lā taʿjal li-amrin turīduhu * wa-kun rāḥiman li-al-nāsi tudʿā bi-rāḥimi
fa-mā min yadin illā yadu Allāhi fawqahā * wa-lā ẓālimin illā sa-yublā bi-ẓālimi
sentences.l:
Be-deliberate, and-not hasten for-a-matter you-want-it, * and-be merciful to-the-people, you-will-be-called by-"merciful";
for-not any hand but the-hand of-God above-it, * and-not a-wrongdoer but will-be-afflicted by-a-wrongdoer.
sentences.i: Go slowly, and do not rush at any matter you desire; be merciful to people, and you will be called merciful. For there is no hand that God's hand is not above, and no wrongdoer who will not be afflicted by another wrongdoer.
sentences.n: تَانَّ stands for تَأَنَّ, "be deliberate"; the print gives it no hamza. The rhyme is -mi, and the printed final kasra on رَاحِمِ and ظَالِمِ (without tanwīn) is kept.

sentences.t: آلْوَصِيَّةُ الثَّالِثَةُ اِلْزَمِ الصَّمْتَ وَاشْتَغِلْ بِعَيْبِكَ عَنْ عُيُوبِ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: al-waṣiyyatu al-thālithatu ilzami al-ṣamta wa-ishtaghil bi-ʿaybika ʿan ʿuyūbi al-nāsi
sentences.l: The-charge the-third: cling-to the-silence, and-busy-yourself with-your-fault away-from the-faults of-the-people.
sentences.i: The third charge: hold to silence, and busy yourself with your own faults rather than with other people's.

sentences.t: فَقَدْ قِيلَ مَنْ لَزِمَ الصَّمْتَ نَجَا
sentences.tr: fa-qad qīla man lazima al-ṣamta najā
sentences.l: For it-was-said: whoever clung-to the-silence was-saved.
sentences.i: For it has been said: whoever holds to silence is saved.

sentences.t: وَسَمِعْتُ الشَّاعِرَ يَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: wa-samiʿtu al-shāʿira yaqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: And-I-heard the-poet saying verse:
sentences.i: And I have heard the poet say in verse:

sentences.t:
الصَّمْتُ زَيْنٌ وَالسُّكُوتُ سَلَامَةٌ * فَاِذَا نَطَقْتَ فَلَا تَكُنْ مِهْذَارًا
فَلَئِنْ نَدِمْتَ عَلَى سُكُوتِكَ مَرَّةً * فَلَتَنْدَمَنَّ عَلَى الْكَلَامِ مِرَارًا
sentences.tr:
al-ṣamtu zaynun wa-al-sukūtu salāmatun * fa-idhā naṭaqta fa-lā takun mihdhāran
fa-la-in nadimta ʿalā sukūtika marratan * fa-la-tandamanna ʿalā al-kalāmi mirāran
sentences.l:
The-silence an-adornment and-the-quiet safety, * so-when you-speak, then not be a-babbler;
so-if indeed you-regret over your-silence once, * then-you-will-surely-regret over the-speech many-times.
sentences.i: Silence is an adornment, and quiet is safety; so when you speak, do not be a babbler. If you regret your silence once, you will surely regret your speech many times over.
sentences.n: Both lines rhyme on -ārā (مِهْذَارًا, مِرَارًا). لَتَنْدَمَنَّ has the emphatic -anna ending, "you will surely regret".

sentences.t: آلرَّابِعَةُ يَا وَلَدِي أُحَذِّرُكَ مِنْ شُرْبِ الْخَمْرِ فَإِنَّ الْخَمْرَ رأْسُ كُلِّ فِتْنَةٍ
sentences.tr: al-rābiʿatu yā waladī uḥadhdhiruka min shurbi al-khamri fa-inna al-khamra raʾsu kulli fitnatin
sentences.l: The-fourth: O my-son, I-warn-you from the-drinking of-the-wine; for indeed the-wine the-head of-every temptation.
sentences.i: The fourth: my son, I warn you against drinking wine; for wine is the head of every trial.

sentences.t: وَالْخَمْرُ مُذْهِبُ الْعُقُولِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-khamru mudhhibu al-ʿuqūli
sentences.l: And-the-wine a-taker-away of-the-minds.
sentences.i: And wine takes the wits away.

sentences.t: الْحَذَرَ الْحَذَرَ مِنْ شُرْبِ الْخَمْرِ لِأَنِّي سَمِعْتُ الشَّاعِرَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: al-ḥadhara al-ḥadhara min shurbi al-khamri li-annī samiʿtu al-shāʿira yaqūlu
sentences.l: The-caution, the-caution from the-drinking of-the-wine, because-I heard the-poet saying:
sentences.i: Beware, beware of drinking wine, for I have heard the poet say:
sentences.n: الْحَذَرَ الْحَذَرَ is the doubled accusative of urgent warning, "beware, beware!"

sentences.t:
تَرَكْتُ النَّبِيذَ وَشُرَّابَهُ * وَصِرْتُ حَلِيفًا لِمَنْ عَابَهُ
شَرَابٌ يُضِلُّ سَبِيلَ الْهُدَى * وَيَفْتَحُ لِلشَّرِّ اَبْوَابَهُ
sentences.tr:
taraktu al-nabīdha wa-shurrābahu * wa-ṣirtu ḥalīfan li-man ʿābahu
sharābun yuḍillu sabīla al-hudā * wa-yaftaḥu li-al-sharri abwābahu
sentences.l:
I-left the-wine and-its-drinkers, * and-became an-ally to-whoever censured-it;
a-drink that-leads-astray the-path of-guidance, * and-opens for-the-evil its-doors.
sentences.i: I have given up wine and those who drink it, and have become the ally of whoever condemns it: a drink that leads the road of guidance astray and opens all its doors to evil.
sentences.n: نَبِيذ is any fermented drink, so here wine. Both lines rhyme on -ābahu.

sentences.t: وَالْخَامِسَةُ يَا وَلَدِي مِنْ مَالِكَ يَصُونُكَ احْفَظْ مَالَكَ يَحْفَظْكَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-khāmisatu yā waladī min mālika yaṣūnuka iḥfaẓ mālaka yaḥfaẓka
sentences.l: And-the-fifth: O my-son, from your-property it-protects-you; guard your-property, it-guards-you.
sentences.i: The fifth: my son, your wealth is what protects you; guard your wealth and it will guard you.
sentences.n: مِنْ مَالِكَ يَصُونُكَ is elliptical; I take it as "your own property will protect you", but the sense is not certain.

sentences.t: وَلَا تُفَرِّطْ فِي مَالِكَ تَحْتَاجْ إِلَى أَقَلِّ النَّاسِ مِنَ الدَّرَاهِمِ فَهِيَ الْمَرَاهِمُ
sentences.tr: wa-lā tufarriṭ fī mālika taḥtāj ilā aqalli al-nāsi mina al-darāhimi fa-hiya al-marāhimu
sentences.l: And-not you-neglect in your-property, you-need to the-least of-the-people in dirhams, for-they the-salves.
sentences.i: Do not squander your wealth, or you will need even the poorest of men; for dirhams are the salves.
sentences.n: A wordplay: الدَّرَاهِم, dirhams, and الْمَرَاهِم, salves, rhyme, the coins being the ointment for life's wounds. As in the second counsel, the print keeps the long vowel in the jussive تَحْتَاجْ.

sentences.t: لِأَنِّي سَمِعْتُ بَعْضَهُمْ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: li-annī samiʿtu baʿḍahum yaqūlu
sentences.l: Because-I heard some-of-them saying:
sentences.i: For I have heard one of them say:

sentences.t:
اِنْ قَلَّ مَالِي فَلَاخِلَّ يُصَاحِبُنِي * وَاِنْ زَادَ مَالِي فَكُلُّ النَّاسِ خُلَّانِي
فَكَمْ صَدِيقٍ لِبَذْلِ الْمَالِ صَاحَبَنِي * وَصَاحِبِي عِنْدَ فَقْدِ الْمَالِ خَلَّانِي
sentences.tr:
in qalla mālī fa-lākhilla yuṣāḥibunī * wa-in zāda mālī fa-kullu al-nāsi khullānī
fa-kam ṣadīqin li-badhli al-māli ṣāḥabanī * wa-ṣāḥibī ʿinda faqdi al-māli khallānī
sentences.l:
If lessens my-wealth, then-no friend keeps-company-with-me, * and-if increases my-wealth, then all the-people my-friends;
for how-many a-friend for the-spending of-the-wealth befriended-me, * and-my-companion at the-loss of-the-wealth left-me.
sentences.i: If my money dwindles, no friend keeps me company; if my money grows, all men are my friends. How many a friend has befriended me for the sake of my spending, while my own companion, when the money was lost, forsook me.
sentences.n: The last word of each line plays on two roots: خُلَّانِي, "my friends", and خَلَّانِي, "left me". The poem rhymes on -ānī.

sentences.t: وَمَازَالَ نُورُالدِّينِ يُوصِي بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ حَتَّى طَلَعَتْ رُوحُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-māzāla Nūru al-Dīni yūṣī Badra al-Dīni Ḥasana ḥattā ṭalaʿat rūḥuhu
sentences.l: And-not he-ceased Nūr al-Dīn charging Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, until went-up his-spirit,
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn went on giving counsel to Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan until his soul departed,
sentences.n: The edition prints the names joined (نورالدين، بدرالدين); they are two words each. The name حَسَنَ is printed without a case alif, so I give it a bare fatḥa.

sentences.t: وَ أَقَامَ الْحُزْنَ فِي بَيْتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-aqāma al-ḥuzna fī baytihi
sentences.l: and he-set-up the-grief in his-house,
sentences.i: and Badr al-Dīn held mourning in his house,
sentences.n: The edition breaks the word وَأَقَامَ across the line, leaving a lone و at the end of the previous line; read it as one word. The subject, Badr al-Dīn, is understood from the previous unit.

sentences.t: وَحَزِنَ عَلَيْهِ السُّلْطَانُ وَجَمِيعُ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَدَفَنُوهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥazina ʿalayhi al-sulṭānu wa-jamīʿu al-umarāʾi wa-dafanūhu
sentences.l: and grieved over-him the-Sultan and all the-emirs, and they-buried-him.
sentences.i: The Sultan grieved for him, and all the emirs, and they buried him.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ بَدْرُالدِّينِ عَلَى وَالِدِهِ فِي حُزْنٍ مُدَّةَ شَهْرَيْنِ وَهُوَ لَمْ يَرْكَبْ وَ لَمْ يَطْلَعِ الدِّيوَانَ وَلَمْ يُقَابِلِ السُّلْطَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal Badru al-Dīni ʿalā wālidihi fī ḥuznin muddata shahrayni wa-huwa lam yarkab wa lam yaṭlaʿi al-dīwāna wa-lam yuqābili al-sulṭāna
sentences.l: And-not he-ceased Badr al-Dīn over his-father in grief a-period-of two-months, and-he not he-rode, and not he-went-up-to the-court, and-not he-met the-Sultan.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn remained in grief over his father for two months; he did not ride out, did not go up to the court, and did not call on the Sultan.
sentences.n: لَمْ يَطْلَعِ الدِّيوَانَ: the court is a place one 'goes up' to, and the verb takes it directly. The edition again splits a word at a line end, leaving a lone و before لَمْ.

sentences.t: فَاغْتَاظَ السُّلْطَانُ عَلَيْهِ فَأَقَامَ مَكَانَهُ بَعْضَ الْحُجَّابِ وَأَجْلَسَهُ وَزِيرًا وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَخْتِمَ عَلَى أَمَاكِنِ نُورِالدِّينِ وَعَلَى مَالِهِ وَعِمَارَتِهِ وَأَمْلَاكِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ightāẓa al-sulṭānu ʿalayhi fa-aqāma makānahu baʿḍa al-ḥujjābi wa-ajlasahu wazīran wa-amarahu an yakhtima ʿalā amākini Nūri al-Dīni wa-ʿalā mālihi wa-ʿimāratihi wa-amlākihi
sentences.l: So became-enraged the-Sultan at-him, so he-set-up in-his-place some-of the-chamberlains, and-seated-him as-vizier, and-commanded-him to he-seal upon the-places of-Nūr al-Dīn, and upon his-wealth and-his-buildings and-his-properties.
sentences.i: The Sultan was enraged with him and set up in his place one of the chamberlains, seating him as vizier, and ordered him to put the seal on Nūr al-Dīn's premises, and on his wealth, his buildings and his estates.
sentences.n: Putting one's seal on a house and its goods (خَتَمَ عَلَى) was how the ruler took an estate into his own hands. بَعْضَ الْحُجَّابِ is 'some of the chamberlains', that is, one of them.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ الْوَزِيرُ الْجَدِيدُ يَخْتِمُ عَلَيْهِ وَيَقْبِضُ عَلَى وَالِدِهِ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ وَيَطْلَعُ بِهِ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ يَعْمَلُ فِيهِ مَا يَقْتَضِي رَأْيُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala al-wazīru al-jadīdu yakhtimu ʿalayhi wa-yaqbiḍu ʿalā wālidihi Badri al-Dīni Ḥasanin wa-yaṭlaʿu bihi ilā al-sulṭāni yaʿmalu fīhi mā yaqtaḍī raʾyuhu
sentences.l: So went-down the-vizier the-new, sealing upon-it, and-seizing upon his-father Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and-going-up with-him to the-Sultan, he-does in-him what requires his-opinion.
sentences.i: So the new vizier went down to seal up the house, to seize Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan and bring him up to the Sultan, who would do with him whatever he saw fit.
sentences.n: As printed, وَالِدِهِ means 'his father', which cannot be right beside the name Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, the dead vizier's son; a later line has وَلَدِهِ 'his son'. It is probably a slip in the edition, but I vocalise what is printed. In مَا يَقْتَضِي رَأْيُهُ ('what his opinion requires') the pronoun that Classical Arabic would add after the verb is left out.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ بَيْنَ الْعَسْكَرِ مَمْلُوكٌ مِنْ مَمَالِيكِ الْوَزِيرِ الْمُتَوَفَّى
sentences.tr: wa-kāna bayna al-ʿaskari mamlūkun min mamālīki al-wazīri al-mutawaffā
sentences.l: And was among the-soldiery a-mamluk from the-mamluks of-the-vizier the-deceased.
sentences.i: Now among the troops there was a mamluk, one of the late vizier's mamluks.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ بِهَذِهِ الْقَضِيَّةِ سَاقَ جَرَادَهُ وَأَتَى مُسْرِعًا إِلَى بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ فَوَجَدَهُ جَالِسًا عَلَى بَابِ دَارِهِ وَهُوَ مُنَكِّسُ الرَّأْسِ حَزِينٌ مُنْكَسِرُ الْقَلْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa bi-hādhihi al-qaḍiyyati sāqa jarādahu wa-atā musriʿan ilā Badri al-Dīni Ḥasanin fa-wajadahu jālisan ʿalā bābi dārihi wa-huwa munakkisu al-raʾsi ḥazīnun munkasiru al-qalbi
sentences.l: So when he-heard of this the-case, he-drove his-'locust' (read: steed), and-came hurrying to Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and-found-him sitting upon door-of his-house, and-he lowering-of the-head, sorrowful, broken-of the-heart.
sentences.i: When he heard of this affair, he spurred his horse and came in haste to Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and found him sitting at the door of his house, head bowed, sorrowful, broken-hearted.
sentences.n: جَرَادَهُ as printed would be 'his locust' (jarād); the sense wants 'his steed', so it is probably a misprint for جَوَادَهُ. I vocalise the letters as printed. سَمِعَ بِـ is 'hear of' (the verb chooses the preposition).

sentences.t: فَتَرَجَّلَ لَهُ الْمَمْلُوكُ وَقُبِّلَتْ يَدُهُ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَاسَيِّدِي وَابْنَ سَيِّدِي الْعَجَلَ الْعَجَلَ قَبْلَ حُلُولِ الْأَجَلِ
sentences.tr: fa-tarajjala lahu al-mamlūku wa-qubbilat yaduhu wa-qāla lahu yāsayyidī wa-ibna sayyidī al-ʿajala al-ʿajala qabla ḥulūli al-ajali
sentences.l: So he-dismounted for-him, the-mamluk, and was-kissed his-hand, and-said to-him: O-my-master and-son-of my-master, the-haste, the-haste, before arrival-of the-term!
sentences.i: The mamluk dismounted before him and kissed his hand, and said to him: My master, son of my master, quick, quick, before the hour of doom arrives!
sentences.n: I read the printed وقبلت يده as the passive وَقُبِّلَتْ يَدُهُ, 'and his hand was kissed'; the active وَقَبَّلَ would be the usual way to say 'he kissed his hand', and the print may have a slip. Either way it is the mamluk who kisses it. الْعَجَلَ الْعَجَلَ is the accusative of urging: 'hurry, hurry'. الْأَجَلُ is the fixed term of a life.

sentences.t: فَارْتَجَفَ حَسَنٌ وَقَالَ مَا الْخَبَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-irtajafa Ḥasanun wa-qāla mā al-khabaru
sentences.l: So trembled Ḥasan, and-said: What the-news?
sentences.i: Ḥasan shook, and said: What is the news?

sentences.t: قَالَ السُّلْطَانُ غَضِبَ عَلَيْكَ وَرَسَمَ بِالْحَوْطَةِ عَلَيْكَ وَالْبَلَاءُ يَجِي مِنْ خَلْفِي إِلَيْكَ فَفُزْ بِنَفْسِكَ
sentences.tr: qāla al-sulṭānu ghaḍiba ʿalayka wa-rasama bi-al-ḥawṭati ʿalayka wa-al-balāʾu yajī min khalfī ilayka fa-fuz bi-nafsika
sentences.l: He-said: The-Sultan became-angry upon-you, and-decreed with-the-seizure upon-you; and the-affliction comes from behind-me to-you; so win with-your-self.
sentences.i: He said: The Sultan is angry with you and has ordered your goods seized, and calamity is coming for you close behind me. Save yourself!
sentences.n: يَجِي is the spelling of يَجِيءُ ('comes') without its hamza, a Middle Arabic form that I vocalise as printed. الْحَوْطَةُ is 'custody, seizure', and رَسَمَ بِـ is 'decree, order (something)'. فُزْ بِنَفْسِكَ, 'win with your self', means 'get away with your life'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ هَلْ فِى الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ حَتَّى أَدْخُلَ إِلَى بَيْتِي أَصْحَبَ شَيْئًا مِنَ الدُّنْيَا أَسْتَعِينَ بِهِ عَلَى الْغُرْبَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu hal fī al-amri shayʾun ḥattā adkhula ilā baytī aṣḥaba shayʾan mina al-dunyā astaʿīna bihi ʿalā al-ghurbati
sentences.l: So he-said to-him: Is-there in the-matter anything, until I-enter to my-house, I-take-along something from the-world, I-seek-help with-it upon the-exile?
sentences.i: Then he said to him: Is there room in the matter for me to go into my house and take along something of this world's goods to help me through exile?
