sentences.n: هَلْ فِى الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ ('is there anything in the matter?') asks whether any room or time is left. فِى is printed with a dotless ى. The three verbs أَدْخُلَ، أَصْحَبَ، أَسْتَعِينَ follow one another with no connecting word, each carrying on the purpose of the one before.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْمَمْلُوكُ يَا سَيِّدِي قُمِ الْآنَ وَخَلِّ عَنْكَ الدَّارَ فَنَهَضَ وَهُوَيَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-mamlūku yā sayyidī qumi al-āna wa-khalli ʿanka al-dāra fa-nahaḍa wa-huwa yaqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: So said the-mamluk: O my-master, rise now, and-leave from-you the-house. So he-rose, and-he saying poetry:
sentences.i: The mamluk said: My master, get up now and leave the house behind you. So he rose, reciting verses as he went:
sentences.n: The edition prints وهويقول as one word.

sentences.t:
وَنَفْسَكَ فُزْ بِهَا إِنْ صِبْتَ ضَيْمًا * وَخَلِّ الدَّارَ تَنْعَى مَنْ بَنَاهَا
فَإِنَّكَ وَاجِدٌ اَرْضًا بِاَرْضٍ * وَنَفْسَكَ لَمْ تَجِدْ نَفْسًا سِوَاهَا
وَلَا تَبْعَثْ رَسُولَكَ فِي مُهِمٍّ * فَمَا لِلنَّفْسِ نَاصِحَةٌ سِوَاهَا
وَمَا غَلُظَتْ رِقَابُ الْاُسْدِ حَتَّى * بِاَنْفُسِهَا تَوَلَّتْ مَا عَنَاهَا
sentences.tr:
wa-nafsaka fuz bihā in ṣibta ḍayman * wa-khalli al-dāra tanʿā man banāhā
fa-innaka wājidun arḍan bi-arḍin * wa-nafsaka lam tajid nafsan siwāhā
wa-lā tabʿath rasūlaka fī muhimmin * fa-mā li-al-nafsi nāṣiḥatun siwāhā
wa-mā ghaluẓat riqābu al-usdi ḥattā * bi-anfusihā tawallat mā ʿanāhā
sentences.l:
And your-self, win with-it, if you-are-struck by-wrong, * and leave the-house, it-announcing-the-death-of him-who built-it;
for indeed-you finding land for land, * and your-self not you-find a-self besides-it.
And not you-send your-messenger in an-important-matter, * for not for-the-self an-adviser besides-it.
And not grew-thick the-necks of-the-lions until * by-their-selves they-took-charge-of what concerned-them.
sentences.i: Save your own self, if wrong strikes you, and leave the house to mourn the one who built it; for you will find one land in place of another, but for your self you will find no other self. Send no messenger on a matter of weight, for no one counsels the self more faithfully than itself. The necks of lions grew thick only when they saw to their own affairs themselves.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse and the pointing is kept as printed, including its bare-alif hamzas (اَرْضًا، بِاَرْضٍ، الْاُسْدِ، بِاَنْفُسِهَا). I read صِبْتَ as a passive of صَابَ, 'you are struck (by wrong)'; the form is unusual, so take that as my best reading. تَنْعَى is 'announces the death of', so the house is left to lament its builder. Each line ends in -hā. The moral is that a man must save himself and attend to his own business in person.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ كَلَامَ الْمَمْلُوكِ غَطَّى رَأْسَهُ بِذَيْلِهِ وَخَرَجَ يَمْشِي إِلَى أَنْ صَارَ خَارِجَ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa kalāma al-mamlūki ghaṭṭā raʾsahu bi-dhaylihi wa-kharaja yamshī ilā an ṣāra khārija al-madīnati
sentences.l: So when he-heard speech-of the-mamluk, he-covered his-head with-his-hem, and-went-out walking until he-became outside the-city.
sentences.i: When he heard the mamluk's words, he covered his head with his hem and went out on foot until he was outside the city.

sentences.t: فَسَمِعَ النَّاسَ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ السُّلْطَانَ أَرْسَلَ الْوَزِيرَ الْجَدِيدَ إِلَى بَيْتِ وَزِيرِهِ الْمُتَوَفَّى يَخْتِمُ عَلَى مَالِهِ وَأَمَاكِنِهِ وَيَقْبِضُ عَلَى وَلَدِهِ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ وَيَطْلَعُ بِهِ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ لِيَقْتُلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-samiʿa al-nāsa yaqūlūna inna al-sulṭāna arsala al-wazīra al-jadīda ilā bayti wazīrihi al-mutawaffā yakhtimu ʿalā mālihi wa-amākinihi wa-yaqbiḍu ʿalā waladihi Badri al-Dīni Ḥasanin wa-yaṭlaʿu bihi ilā al-sulṭāni li-yaqtulahu
sentences.l: So he-heard the-people saying: Indeed the-Sultan sent the-vizier the-new to house-of his-vizier the-deceased, sealing upon his-wealth and-his-premises, and-seizing upon his-son Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and-going-up with-him to the-Sultan, in-order-that-he-kill-him.
sentences.i: Then he heard the people saying that the Sultan had sent the new vizier to the house of his late vizier to seal up his wealth and his premises, to seize his son Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan and bring him up to the Sultan, so that he might put him to death.
sentences.n: Here the text says وَلَدِهِ, 'his son', where the earlier line, as printed, has وَالِدِهِ.

sentences.t: فَتَأَسَّفَ النَّاسُ عَلَى حُسْنِهِ وَجَمَالِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-taʾassafa al-nāsu ʿalā ḥusnihi wa-jamālihi
sentences.l: So grieved the-people over his-beauty and-his-comeliness.
sentences.i: And the people grieved over his beauty and comeliness.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ كَلَامَ النَّاسِ خَرَجَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَيْنَ يَذْهَبُ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ سَائِرًا إِلَى أَنْ سَاقَتْهُ الْمَقَادِيرُ عَلَى تُرْبَةِ وَالِدِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa kalāma al-nāsi kharaja ʿalā raʾsihi wa-lam yaʿlam ayna yadhhabu wa-lam yazal sāʾiran ilā an sāqathu al-maqādīru ʿalā turbati wālidihi
sentences.l: So when he-heard speech-of the-people, he-went-out upon his-head, and-not he-knew where he-goes, and-not he-ceased travelling until drove-him the-decrees upon tomb-of his-father.
sentences.i: When he heard what the people said, he went out headlong, not knowing where to go, and kept walking until the decrees of fate brought him to his father's tomb.
sentences.n: خَرَجَ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ, 'went out on his head', is an idiom for setting out headlong, with no plan. الْمَقَادِيرُ are the divine decrees, fate.

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ الْمَقْبَرَةَ وَشَقَّ بَيْنَ الْقُبُورِ إِلَى أَنْ جَلَسَ إِلَى قَبْرِ أَبِيهِ وَأَرْخَى ذَيْلَ فَرَجِيَّتِهِ مِنْ فَوْقِ رَأْسِهِ وَكَانَتْ مَنْسُوجَةً بِطِرَازِ ذَهَبٍ مَكْتُوبًا عَلَيْهَا هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتُ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala al-maqbarata wa-shaqqa bayna al-qubūri ilā an jalasa ilā qabri abīhi wa-arkhā dhayla farajiyyatihi min fawqi raʾsihi wa-kānat mansūjatan bi-ṭirāzi dhahabin maktūban ʿalayhā hādhihi al-abyātu
sentences.l: So he-entered the-cemetery, and-cleft between the-graves until he-sat by tomb-of his-father, and-let-down hem-of his-robe from above his-head; and-it-was woven with-a-band-of gold, written upon-it these the-verses:
sentences.i: He entered the cemetery and made his way among the graves until he sat down beside his father's tomb, and let the hem of his robe fall over his head. The robe was woven with a band of gold, and on it were written these verses:
sentences.n: فَرَجِيَّة is a long outer robe. طِرَاز is an embroidered band, often carrying an inscription; here it is of gold, and the verses are written on it. بِـ in بِطِرَازِ means 'with'.

sentences.t:
يَا مَنْ لَهُ وَجْهٌ شَرِيقُ * يَحْكِي الْكَوَاكِبَ وَالنَّدَا
لَازَالَ عِزُّكَ دَائِمًا * وَعُلُوُّ مَجْدِكَ سَرْمَدَا
sentences.tr:
yā man lahu wajhun sharīqu * yaḥkī al-kawākiba wa-al-nadā
lā zāla ʿizzuka dāʾiman * wa-ʿuluwwu majdika sarmadā
sentences.l:
O whom to-him a-face shining, * resembling the-stars and-the-dew,
not may-cease your-might lasting, * and-loftiness-of your-glory eternal.
sentences.i: O you whose face shines, like the stars and the dew: may your might endure always, and the loftiness of your glory be everlasting.
sentences.n: The pointing is the edition's own, kept as printed. شَرِيقُ is an obscure form; I take it as 'shining', perhaps from شَرِقَ or أَشْرَقَ, but cannot be sure. النَّدَا means both 'dew' and 'bounty', and either may be meant. The two hemistichs of the first line end -qu and -dā, so the rhymes do not agree in the print.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ عِنْدَ تُرْبَةِ أَبِيهِ إِذْ قَدِمَ عَلَيْهِ يَهُودِيٌّ كَأَنَّهُ صَيْرَ فِيٌّ وَمَعَهُ خُرْجٌ فِيهِ ذَهَبٌ كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā huwa ʿinda turbati abīhi idh qadima ʿalayhi yahūdiyyun ka-annahu ṣayrafiyyun wa-maʿahu khurjun fīhi dhahabun kathīrun
sentences.l: So while he at tomb-of his-father, behold arrived upon-him a-Jew, as-though-he a-money-changer, and with-him a-saddlebag in-it gold much.
sentences.i: While he was beside his father's tomb, a Jew came up to him, looking like a money-changer, with a saddlebag full of gold beside him.
sentences.n: The edition prints صيرفي (ṣayrafī, money-changer) as two words, صير في; it is vocalised here as the single word it evidently is, with the printed space kept. كَأَنَّهُ means "as though he were".

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ الْيَهُودِيُّ إِلَى حَسَنٍ الْبَصْرِيِّ وَقَالَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama al-yahūdiyyu ilā Ḥasanin al-Baṣriyyi wa-qāla lahu
sentences.l: So advanced the-Jew to Ḥasan the-Basran and said to-him:
sentences.i: The Jew stepped up to Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan of Basra and said to him:
sentences.n: Here the text calls him simply Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Ḥasan the Basran, as it will throughout this passage; he is Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan.

sentences.t: يَا سَيِّدِي مَانِي أَرَاكَ مُتَغَيِّرًا
sentences.tr: yā sayyidī mā-nī arāka mutaghayyiran
sentences.l: O my-master, what-I I-see-you altered?
sentences.i: My master, how is it that I see you so changed?
sentences.n: مَانِي is obscure. It looks like a colloquial "how is it with me that ..." (perhaps for مَا لِي or مَا بَالِي), and the sense required is "why do I see you changed?"; the vocalisation follows the printed letters.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ إِنِّي كُنْتُ نَائِمًا فِي هَذِهِالسَّاعَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu innī kuntu nāʾiman fī hādhihi-al-sāʿati
sentences.l: So he-said to-him: Indeed-I I-was sleeping in this-the-hour,
sentences.i: He said to him: I was asleep just now,
sentences.n: هَذِهِالسَّاعَةِ is two words printed run together (هذه + الساعة); the edition does this often. "This hour" means "just now".

sentences.t: فَرَأَيْتُ أَبِي يُعَاتِبُنِي عَلَى عَدَمِ زِيَارَتِي لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-raʾaytu abī yuʿātibunī ʿalā ʿadami ziyāratī lahu
sentences.l: and I-saw my-father he-reproaches-me upon non-existence-of my-visiting to-him;
sentences.i: and I saw my father reproaching me for not having visited him;

sentences.t: فَقُمْتُ وَأَنَا مَرْعُوبٌ وَخِفْتُ أَنْ يَفُوتَ النَّهَارُ وَلَمْ أَزُرْهُ فَيَكُونَ صَعْبًا عَلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qumtu wa-anā marʿūbun wa-khiftu an yafūta al-nahāru wa-lam azurhu fa-yakūna ṣaʿban ʿalayya
sentences.l: so I-rose, and I terrified, and I-feared that passes-away the-day and not I-visit-him, so-that-it-be hard upon-me.
sentences.i: so I rose in terror, fearing that the day would pass before I had visited him, and that it would then go hard with me.
sentences.n: مَرْعُوبٌ "terrified" is a later, non-Classical-looking participle (from رَعَبَ); it is normal in this register. The فَـ before يَكُونَ makes the clause a consequence ("and so it would be hard for me").

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْيَهُودِيُّ يَا سَيِّدِي أَبَاكَ كَانَ أَرْسَلَ مَرَاكِبَ لِلتِّجَارَةِ وَقَدِمَ مِنْهَا الْبَعْضُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-yahūdiyyu yā sayyidī abāka kāna arsala marākiba li-al-tijārati wa-qadima minhā al-baʿḍu
sentences.l: So said to-him the-Jew: O my-master, your-father (acc.) had sent ships for-the-trade, and arrived of-them the-some.
sentences.i: Then the Jew said to him: My lord, your father had sent out ships for trade, and some of them have arrived.
sentences.n: أَبَاكَ is printed in the accusative although it is the subject of كَانَ; this is a Middle Arabic feature and the vocalisation keeps what the letters say.

sentences.t: وَمُرَادِي أَشْتَرِي مِنْكَ وَسْقَ أَوَّلِ مَرْكَبٍ قَدِمَ بِهَذَا الْأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ ذَهَبٍ
sentences.tr: wa-murādī ashtarī minka wasqa awwali markabin qadima bi-hādhā al-alfi dīnārin dhahabin
sentences.l: and my-intention I-buy from-you the-cargo-of first ship arrived with-this the-thousand dinar gold.
sentences.i: and what I want is to buy from you the cargo of the first ship to arrive, for this thousand dinars of gold.
sentences.n: أَشْتَرِي follows مُرَادِي with no أَنْ, as in speech: "my wish: I buy". The وَسْق is a ship's whole load. The article on الْأَلْفِ before دِينَارٍ is another non-Classical touch.

sentences.t: وَأَخْرَجَ الْيَهُودِيُّ كِيسًا مَلْآنَ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَعَدَّمِنْهُ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَأَعْطَاهَا إِلَى حَسَنِ بْنِ الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhraja al-yahūdiyyu kīsan malʾāna mina al-dhahabi wa-ʿaddamin-hu alfa dīnārin wa-aʿṭāhā ilā Ḥasani ibni al-wazīri
sentences.l: And brought-out the-Jew a-purse full of the-gold, and counted-from-it a-thousand dinar, and gave-them to Ḥasan son-of the-vizier.
sentences.i: The Jew drew out a purse full of gold, counted a thousand dinars from it, and handed them to Ḥasan, the vizier's son.
sentences.n: وَعَدَّمِنْهُ is printed as one word: وَ + عَدَّ + مِنْهُ, "and counted out of it".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْيَهُودِيُّ اُكْتُبْ لِي وَرَقَةً وَاخْتِمْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-yahūdiyyu uktub lī waraqatan wa-ukhtimhā
sentences.l: So said the-Jew: Write for-me a-paper, and seal-it.
sentences.i: Then the Jew said: Write me a deed, and seal it.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ حَسَنُ بْنُ الْوَزِيرِ وَرَقَةً وَكَتَبَ فِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha Ḥasanu ibnu al-wazīri waraqatan wa-kataba fīhā
sentences.l: So took Ḥasan son-of the-vizier a-paper, and wrote in-it:
sentences.i: So the vizier's son took a sheet of paper and wrote on it:

sentences.t: كَاتِبُهَا حَسَنُ بْنُ الْوَزِيرِ بَاعَ لِإِسْحَاقَ الْيَهُودِيِّ جَمِيعَ وَسْقِ أَوَّلِ مَرْكَبٍ أَبِيهِ يَدْخُلُ بِأَلْفِ دِينَارٍ وَقَبَضَ الثَّمَنَ عَلَى سَبِيلِ التَّعْجِيلِ
sentences.tr: kātibuhā Ḥasanu ibnu al-wazīri bāʿa li-Isḥāqa al-yahūdiyyi jamīʿa wasqi awwali markabin abīhi yadkhulu bi-alfi dīnārin wa-qabaḍa al-thamana ʿalā sabīli al-taʿjīli
sentences.l: Its-writer Ḥasan son-of the-vizier: he-sold to-Isḥāq the-Jew the-whole of-cargo-of first ship of-his-father that-enters, for a-thousand dinar; and he-received the-price upon way-of the-advance-payment.
sentences.i: The writer, Ḥasan the vizier's son, has sold to Isḥāq the Jew the entire cargo of the first of his father's ships to come into port, for a thousand dinars, and has received the price in advance.
sentences.n: The deed is a sale of goods not yet landed, paid for beforehand. عَلَى سَبِيلِ التَّعْجِيلِ is a stock phrase, "by way of prompt payment".

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الْيَهُودِيُّ الْوَرَقَةَ وَصَارَ حَسَنٌ يَبْكِي وَيَتَذَكَّرُ مَاكَانَ فِيهِ مِنَ الْعِزِّ وَيُنْشِدُ وَيَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-yahūdiyyu al-waraqata wa-ṣāra Ḥasanun yabkī wa-yatadhakkaru mākāna fīhi mina al-ʿizzi wa-yunshidu wa-yaqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: So took the-Jew the-paper, and became Ḥasan weeping, and remembering what was in-it of the-glory, and reciting and saying poetry.
sentences.i: The Jew took the paper, and Ḥasan fell to weeping and remembering the glory he had once lived in, and he recited these verses:
sentences.n: مَاكَانَ is printed as one word (مَا كَانَ, "what he had been in").

sentences.t:
مَا بِالدَّارِ مُذْغِبْتُمْ يَا سَادَتِي دَارُ * كَلَّا وَلَاالْجَارُ مُذْغِبْتُمْ لَنَا جَارُ
وَلَا الْاَنِيسُ الَّذِي قَدْ كُنْتُ اَعْهَدُهُ * بِهَا اَنِيسِي وَلَا الْاَقْمَارُ اَقْمَارُ
sentences.tr:
mā bi-al-dāri mudhghibtum yā sādatī dārun * kallā wa-lā al-jāru mudhghibtum lanā jārun
wa-lā al-anīsu alladhī qad kuntu aʿhaduhu * bihā anīsī wa-lā al-aqmāru aqmārun
sentences.l:
Not in-the-house, since-you-were-absent, O my-masters, a-house; * nay, and-not the-neighbour, since-you-were-absent, for-us a-neighbour,
and-not the-companion who indeed I-was I-knew-him * in-it my-companion, and-not the-moons moons.
sentences.i: Since you went away, my lords, the house is no house, nor is the neighbour any neighbour to us; the friend I used to know there is no friend to me now, and the moons are moons no longer.
sentences.n: The pointing is the edition's own and is kept as printed. مُذْغِبْتُمْ (mudh + ghibtum, "since you were absent") and وَلَاالْجَارُ are printed run together. "The house is no house" means that the place is empty of what made it a home. In the last line, "the moons" are the beloved faces.

sentences.t:
غِبْتُمْ فَاَوْحَشْتُمُ الدُّنْيَا بِبُعْدِكُمُ * وَاَظْلَمَتْ بَعْدَكُمْ رَحْبًا وَاَقْطَارُ
لَيْتَ الْغُرَابَ الَّذِي نَادَى بِفُرْقَتِنَا * يُعْرَا مِنَ الرِّيشِ لَا تَحْوِيهِ اَوْكَارُ
sentences.tr:
ghibtum fa-awḥashtumu al-dunyā bi-buʿdikumu * wa-aẓlamat baʿdakum raḥban wa-aqṭārun
layta al-ghurāba alladhī nādā bi-furqatinā * yuʿrā mina al-rīshi lā taḥwīhi awkārun
sentences.l:
You-were-absent, so you-made-desolate the-world by-your-distance, * and grew-dark after-you a-spacious-land and regions;
O-that the-raven who called with-our-parting * be-stripped of the-feather, not hold-it nests.
sentences.i: You went away and left the world desolate by your absence, and after you the wide land and its regions grew dark. Would that the raven that cried out our parting were stripped of its feathers, and no nests held it!
sentences.n: Pointing as printed. رَحْبًا is printed with the accusative ending though it seems to be a subject ("the wide land"); the printed vowel is kept. The raven (ghurāb) is the bird of separation in Arabic poetry, because its cry was heard as an omen of the beloved's departure, and يُعْرَا is the printed spelling of يُعْرَى.

sentences.t:
قَدْ قَلَّ صَبْرِي وَاَضْنِي بَعْدَكُمْ جِسْمِي * وَكَمْ تَهَتَّكَ يَوْمَ الْبَيْنِ اَسْتَارُ
تَرَى تَعُودُ لَيَالِينَا الَّتِي سَلَفَتْ * كَمَا عَهِدْنَا وَتَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنَا الدَّارُ
sentences.tr:
qad qalla ṣabrī wa-uḍnī baʿdakum jismī * wa-kam tahattaka yawma al-bayni astārun
tarā taʿūdu layālīnā allatī salafat * kamā ʿahidnā wa-tajmaʿu baynanā al-dāru
sentences.l:
Indeed little my-patience, and was-wasted after-you my-body, * and how-many were-torn-open on-day-of the-parting curtains;
Do-you-think will-return our-nights which passed * as we-knew, and will-gather between-us the-abode.
sentences.i: My patience is spent and my body wasted since you left, and how many veils were torn away on the day of parting. Do you think our past nights will return as we knew them, and that the house will bring us together again?
sentences.n: Pointing as printed. اَضْنِي is printed with a fatḥa on its first letter; the verb is أُضْنِيَ, "was worn down" (passive of أَضْنَى), and the printed vowel is kept. "Veils torn away" means that secrets and reserve were laid bare by grief. تَرَى here opens a question, "do you think?".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ وَأَسْنَدَ رَأْسَهُ عَلَى قَبْرَأَبِيهِ فَأَدْرَكَهُ النَّوْمُ
sentences.tr: thumma bakā bukāʾan shadīdan fa-dakhala ʿalayhi al-laylu wa-asnada raʾsahu ʿalā qabra abīhi fa-adrakahu al-nawmu
sentences.l: Then he-wept a-weeping intense; and-entered upon-him the-night, and-he-leaned his-head upon the-grave-of-his-father, and-overtook-him the-sleep.
sentences.i: Then he wept bitterly, and night fell upon him; he leaned his head on his father's grave, and sleep overtook him.
sentences.n: The print runs قبر أبيه "his father's grave" together as one word, قَبْرَأَبِيهِ; I have kept it as printed.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ نَائِمًا حَتَّى طَلَعَ الْقَمَرُ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal nāʾiman ḥattā ṭalaʿa al-qamaru
sentences.l: and-not he-ceased sleeping until rose the-moon,
sentences.i: He went on sleeping until the moon rose,

sentences.t: قَتَلَ حَرَجَتْ رَأْسُهُ عَنِ الْقَبْرِ وَ نَامَ عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ وَصَارَ وَجْهُهُ يَلْمَعُ فِى الْقَمَرِ
sentences.tr: qatala ḥarajat raʾsuhu ʿani al-qabri wa nāma ʿalā ẓahrihi wa-ṣāra wajhuhu yalmaʿu fī al-qamari
sentences.l: [qatala, sic] came-out his-head from the-grave, and he-slept upon his-back, and-became his-face shining in the-moon.
sentences.i: his head had come out of the grave, and he lay on his back, with his face shining in the moonlight.
sentences.n: Two words here look like misprints. قتل as pointed (qatala, "he killed") makes no sense; it may stand for قد "had" or قبل "before", and my English follows the sense "had". حرجت is probably خرجت "came out" with the dot misplaced. I have pointed both as printed. The و at the line end is the prefix of نام, split by the line break: wa-nāma, "and he slept".

sentences.t: وَكَانَتِ الْمَقْبَرَةُ عَامِرَةً مِنَ الْجَانِّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-kānati al-maqbaratu ʿāmiratan mina al-jānni al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: and-was the-cemetery inhabited by the-jinn the-believing-ones.
sentences.i: Now the cemetery was inhabited by believing jinn.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتْ جِبِّيَّةٌ فَنَظَرَتْ حَسَنَ نَائِمًا
sentences.tr: fa-kharajat jibbiyyatun fa-naẓarat ḥasana nāʾiman
sentences.l: and-came-out a-jinn-woman, and-she-looked-at Ḥasan sleeping.
sentences.i: A female jinni came out and saw Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan asleep.
sentences.n: جبية is printed so; it must be a misprint for جنية jinniyya "female jinni", with the dot of nūn misplaced as bāʾ. I point it as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَتْهُ تَعَجَّبَتْ مِنْ حُسْنِهِ وَجَمَالِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾathu taʿajjabat min ḥusnihi wa-jamālihi
sentences.l: and-when she-saw-him she-marvelled at his-beauty and-his-comeliness.
sentences.i: When she saw him she marvelled at his beauty and his grace.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ سُبْحَانَ اللهِ مَا هَذَا الشَّابُّ إِلَّا كَأَنَّهُ مِنْ وِلْدَ انِ الْجَنَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat subḥāna allāhi mā hādhā al-shābbu illā ka-annahu min wilda āni al-jannati
sentences.l: and-she-said: Glory-of God! Not this the-youth except as-if-he from the-youths-of the-Garden.
sentences.i: She said: Glory be to God! This young man is surely one of the youths of Paradise.
sentences.n: The print splits وِلْدَان "youths" into ولد ان; I point the two pieces so that they read wildān together. The wildān al-janna are the beautiful youths who serve the blessed in Paradise.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَارَتْ إِلَى الْجَوِّ تَطُوفُ عَلَى عَٰدَتِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma ṭārat ilā al-jawwi taṭūfu ʿalā ʿādatihā
sentences.l: Then she-flew to the-air, circling upon her-custom,
sentences.i: Then she flew up into the air and went circling, as was her wont,
sentences.n: The print has عدتها; I read عادتها "her custom", and so add the dagger alif. The other possible reading, عِدَّتِهَا "her gear/her company", is less likely.

sentences.t: فَرَأَتْ عِفْرِيتًا طَائِرًا فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-raʾat ʿifrītan ṭāʾiran fa-sallama ʿalayhā
sentences.l: and-she-saw an-ifrit flying, and-he-greeted her.
sentences.i: and she saw an ifrit flying, and he greeted her.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ قَادِمٌ فَقَالَ مِنْ هُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu min ayna anta qādimun fa-qāla min hunā
sentences.l: and-she-said to-him: From where you coming? and-he-said: From here.
sentences.i: She said to him: Where have you come from? He said: From here.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تَرُوحَ مَعِي حَتَّى تَنْظُرَ إِلَى حُسْنِ هَذَا الشَّابِّ النَّائِمِ فِى التُّرْبَةِ فَقَالَ لَهَا نَعَمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu hal laka an tarūḥa maʿī ḥattā tanẓura ilā ḥusni hādhā al-shābbi al-nāʾimi fī al-turbati fa-qāla lahā naʿam
sentences.l: and-she-said to-him: Is-there for-you that you-go with-me until you-look at the-beauty-of this the-youth the-sleeping in the-tomb? and-he-said to-her: Yes.
sentences.i: She said to him: Would you care to come with me and look at the beauty of this young man asleep in the tomb? He said to her: Yes.
sentences.n: هل لك أن means "would you like to", literally "is there for you that".

sentences.t: فَسَارُوا حَتَّى نَزَلُوا عَلَى الْقَبْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-sārū ḥattā nazalū ʿalā al-qabri
sentences.l: and-they-went until they-alighted upon the-grave.
sentences.i: So they went on until they came down at the grave.
sentences.n: The verbs are plural although only two travel; the text does not use the dual here, a common looseness in this register.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ هَلْ رَأَيْتَ فِي عُمْرِكَ مِثْلَ هَذَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat hal raʾayta fī ʿumrika mithla hādhā
sentences.l: and-she-said: Have-you-seen in your-lifetime the-like-of this?
sentences.i: She said: Have you ever in your life seen the like of this?

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ الْعِفْرِيتُ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ لَا شَبِيهَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara al-ʿifrītu ilayhi wa-qāla subḥāna man lā shabīha lahu
sentences.l: and-looked the-ifrit at-him and-said: Glory-of whom no likeness to-him!
sentences.i: The ifrit looked at him and said: Glory be to the One who has no like!
sentences.n: مَنْ لَا شَبِيهَ لَهُ "he who has no likeness" is God.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ يَا أُخْتِي إِنْ أَرَدْتِ أَنْ أُحَدِّثَكِ بِمَا رَأَيْتُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin yā ukhtī in aradti an uḥaddithaki bi-mā raʾaytu
sentences.l: but O my-sister, if you-wished that I-tell-you of-what I-saw,
sentences.i: But, my sister, if you wish me to tell you what I have seen,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ وَمَا هُوَ
sentences.tr: qālat wa-mā huwa
sentences.l: she-said: and-what is-it?
sentences.i: She said: And what is it?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ مِثْلَ هَذَا الشَّابِّ فِي إِقْلِيمِ مِصْرَ وَهِيَ بِنْتُ الْوَزِيرِ شَمْسِ الدِّينِ وَعُمْرُهَا قَرِيبٌ مِنْ عِشْرِينَ سَنَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā innī raʾaytu mithla hādhā al-shābbi fī iqlīmi miṣra wa-hiya bintu al-wazīri shamsi al-dīni wa-ʿumruhā qarībun min ʿishrīna sanatan
sentences.l: and-he-said to-her: Indeed-I I-saw the-like-of this the-youth in the-region-of Egypt, and-she daughter-of the-vizier Shams al-Dīn, and-her-age near from twenty year.
sentences.i: He said to her: I have seen the like of this young man in the land of Egypt, and she is the daughter of the vizier Shams al-Dīn, and she is nearly twenty years old.
sentences.n: The ifrit says "the like of this youth" and then "she": the likeness is of a young woman, and the masculine word is used loosely.

sentences.t: وَلَهَا حُسْنٌ وَجَمَالٌ وَبَهَاءٌ وَكَمَالٌ وَقَدٌّ وَ اعْتِدَالٌ
sentences.tr: wa-lahā ḥusnun wa-jamālun wa-bahāʾun wa-kamālun wa-qaddun wa-iʿtidālun
sentences.l: and-for-her beauty and-comeliness and-radiance and-perfection and-stature and symmetry.
sentences.i: She has beauty and grace, radiance and perfection, a fine stature and a perfect symmetry.
sentences.n: The print breaks the line after a lone و, which belongs to اعتدال (wa-iʿtidāl). I read وقد as وَقَدٌّ qadd, "stature", since the list of nouns calls for it; the alternative, وَقَدْ "and already", does not fit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَتْ هَذَا السِّنَّ سَمِعَ بِهَا السُّلْطَانُ بِمِصْرَ فَأَحْضَرَ الْوَزِيرَ أَبَاهَا وَقَالَ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jāwazat hādhā al-sinna samiʿa bihā al-sulṭānu bi-miṣra fa-aḥḍara al-wazīra abāhā wa-qāla lahu
sentences.l: and-when she-passed this the-age, heard of-her the-Sultan in-Egypt; and-he-summoned the-vizier her-father and-said to-him:
sentences.i: When she passed this age, the Sultan in Egypt heard of her; he summoned the vizier, her father, and said to him:

sentences.t: اِعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ أَنَّهُ بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ لَكَ بِنْتٌ وَأَنَا أُرِيدُ أَخْطُبُهَا مِنْكَ
sentences.tr: iʿlam ayyuhā al-wazīru annahu balaghanī anna laka bintun wa-anā urīdu akhṭubuhā minka
sentences.l: Know, O vizier, that-it it-reached-me that for-you a-daughter, and-I desiring I-ask-for-her from-you.
sentences.i: Know, vizier, that word has reached me that you have a daughter, and I wish to ask her hand of you.
sentences.n: Two features of this register. After أَنَّ the Classical form would be the accusative بِنْتًا, but the print has no alif, so I point it bintun. And أُرِيدُ أَخْطُبُهَا puts one verb after another without أَنْ: "I want, I ask for her".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ يَا مَوْلَانَا السُّلْطَانُ اقْبَلْ عُذْرِي وَارْحَمْ عَبْرَتِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru yā mawlānā al-sulṭānu iqbal ʿudhrī wa-irḥam ʿabratī
sentences.l: and-said to-him the-vizier: O our-master the-Sultan, accept my-excuse and-have-mercy-on my-tear.
sentences.i: The vizier said to him: Our lord the Sultan, accept my excuse and have pity on my tears.
sentences.n: عَبْرَة is a tear, or the tears of weeping.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّكَ تَعْرِفُ أَنَّ أَخِي نُورَالدِّينِ خَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِنَا وَلَا نَعْلَمُ أَيْنَ هُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-innaka taʿrifu anna akhī nūra al-dīni kharaja min ʿindinā wa-lā naʿlamu ayna huwa
sentences.l: for-indeed-you you-know that my-brother Nūr al-Dīn went-out from with-us, and-not we-know where he.
sentences.i: For you know that my brother Nūr al-Dīn left us, and we do not know where he is.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ شَرِيكِي فِى الْوِزَارَةِ وَأَصْلُ خُرُوجِهِ غَضْبَانَ لِأَنِّي جَلَسْتُ وَإِيَّاهُ وَحَدَّثْتُهُ عَلَى سَبَبِ الزَّوَاجِ وَالْأَوْلَادِ فَكَانَ سَبَبًا لِغَيْظِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna sharīkī fī al-wizārati wa-aṣlu khurūjihi ghaḍbāna li-annī jalastu wa-iyyāhu wa-ḥaddathtuhu ʿalā sababi al-zawāji wa-al-awlādi fa-kāna sababan li-ghayẓihi
sentences.l: and-he-was my-partner in the-vizierate, and-the-origin-of his-going-out angry, because-I I-sat and-him and-I-talked-to-him on the-cause-of the-marriage and-the-children, and-it-was a-cause for-his-rage.
sentences.i: He was my partner in the vizierate, and the root of his leaving, angry, was that I sat with him and spoke to him about marriage and children, and that became the cause of his fury.
sentences.n: أَصْلُ خُرُوجِهِ غَضْبَانَ is elliptical: "the root of his departure was that he left angry". جَلَسْتُ وَإِيَّاهُ is "I sat, and he", that is, I sat with him.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا حَالِفٌ لَأُزَوِّجُ بِنْتِي إِلَّا لِابْنِ أَخِي مِنْ يَوْمِ وَلَدَتْهَا أُمُّهَا نَحْوَ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً
sentences.tr: wa-anā ḥālifun lā uzawwiju bintī illā li-ibni akhī min yawmi waladathā ummuhā naḥwa thamāniyata ʿashara sanatan
sentences.l: and-I swearing: not I-marry-off my-daughter except to-the-son-of my-brother, from the-day bore-her her-mother, about eighteen year.
sentences.i: I have sworn that I will give my daughter in marriage to no one but my brother's son, from the day her mother bore her, some eighteen years ago.
sentences.n: The print has one alif in لازوج, which has to serve for both لَا and أُزَوِّجُ; I read it lā uzawwiju, "I will not marry off". The "eighteen" here does not quite agree with the ifrit's "nearly twenty" above, but the text says both.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ مُدَّةٍ قَرِيبَةٍ سَمِعْتُ أَنَّ أَخِي تَزَوَّجَ بِنْتَ الْوَزِيرِ بَتَاعِ الْبَصْرَةِ وَجَا مِنْهَا وَلَدًا وَلَا أُزَوِّجُ بِنْتِي إِلَّا لَهُ كَرَامَةً لِأَخِي
sentences.tr: wa-min muddatin qarībatin samiʿtu anna akhī tazawwaja binta al-wazīri bitāʿi al-baṣrati wa-jā minhā waladan wa-lā uzawwiju bintī illā lahu karāmatan li-akhī
sentences.l: and-from a-time near I-heard that my-brother married the-daughter-of the-vizier belonging-to Basra, and-came from-her a-son, and-not I-marry-off my-daughter except to-him, as-an-honour to-my-brother.
sentences.i: Not long ago I heard that my brother had married the daughter of the vizier of Basra, and that a son had come of her; and I will marry my daughter to no one but him, in honour of my brother.
sentences.n: بتاع "belonging to" is Egyptian colloquial, and جَا for جاء "came" is colloquial too. وَلَدًا is accusative as printed, as if the son were the object of "came".

sentences.t: وَأَرَّخْتُ زَوَاجِي وَحَمْلَ زَوْجَتِي وَوِلَادَةَ هَذِهِ الْبِنْتِ وَهِىَ عَلَى اسْمِ ابْنِ عَمِّهَا وَالْبَنَاتُ لِمَوْلَانَا السُّلْطَانِ كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-arrakhtu zawājī wa-ḥamla zawjatī wa-wilādata hādhihi al-binti wa-hiya ʿalā ismi ibni ʿammihā wa-al-banātu li-mawlānā al-sulṭāni kathīrun
sentences.l: and-I-dated my-marriage and-the-pregnancy-of my-wife and-the-birth-of this the-girl, and-she upon the-name-of the-son-of her-paternal-uncle; and-the-girls to-our-master the-Sultan many.
sentences.i: I have kept the dates of my marriage, my wife's pregnancy and this girl's birth, and she stands in the name of her cousin; and our lord the Sultan has girls in plenty.
sentences.n: وَأَرَّخْتُ is uncertain: I read it as "I dated, I recorded the date of", but the verb may be a corruption of أَخَّرْتُ "I put off, delayed". على اسم ابن عمها "on the name of her cousin" means that she is reserved for him. The Sultan "has many girls" is li- of possession.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ السُّلْطَانُ كَلَامَ الْوَزِيرِ غَضِبَ غَضَبًا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-sulṭānu kalāma al-wazīri ghaḍiba ghaḍaban shadīdan
sentences.l: and-when heard the-Sultan the-speech-of the-vizier, he-was-angry an-anger intense.
sentences.i: When the Sultan heard the vizier's words, he flew into a great rage.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ مِثْلِي مَنْ يَخْطُبُ مِنْ مِثْلِكَ بِنْتًا تَمْنَهَا وَتَحْتَجُّ بِحُجَّةٍ بَارِدَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla mithlī man yakhṭubu min mithlika bintan tamnahā wa-taḥtajju bi-ḥujjatin bāridatin
sentences.l: and-he-said: The-like-of-me, who asks from the-like-of-you a-daughter, you-[withhold]-her and-you-plead with-a-plea cold!
sentences.i: He said: Is it for one such as I to ask of one such as you for a daughter, and you refuse her and plead some feeble pretext?
sentences.n: تمنها is obscure. I take it as a misprint for تَمْنَعُهَا "you withhold her", with the ʿayn dropped, and point it as printed. باردة "cold" says the excuse is feeble.

sentences.t: وَحَبْوَةِ رَأْسِي لَا أُزَوِّجُهَا إِلَّا لِأَقَلِّ خَدَمِي رَغْمًا عَنْ أَنْفِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥabwati raʾsī lā uzawwijuhā illā li-aqalli khadamī raghman ʿan anfika
sentences.l: and-by-the-[life]-of my-head, not I-marry-her-off except to-the-least-of my-servants, in-spite from your-nose!
sentences.i: By the life of my head, I will marry her to the lowliest of my servants and to no one else, in spite of you!
sentences.n: حبوة looks like a misprint for حَيْوَة (حياة) "life", with bāʾ for yāʾ: وحياة رأسي "by the life of my head" is an oath. رغما عن أنفك "in spite of your nose" means "to your humiliation, whether you like it or not".

sentences.t: وَكَانَ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ سَائِسٌ أَحْدَبُ بِحَدْبَةٍ مِنْ قُدَّامٍ وَحَدْبَةٍ مِنْ وَرَاءِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ʿinda al-maliki sāʾisun aḥdabu bi-ḥadbatin min quddāmin wa-ḥadbatin min warāʾihā
sentences.l: and-there-was with the-king a-groom, a-hunchback, with-a-hump from front and-a-hump from behind-it.
sentences.i: Now the Sultan had a hunchbacked groom, with a hump in front and a hump behind.
sentences.n: وراءها is printed with the feminine pronoun, "from behind it"; the pronoun looks back to the groom's body, and I point it as a genitive after مِنْ.

sentences.t: فَأَمَرَ السُّلْطَانُ بِإِحْضَارِهِ وَكَتَبَ كِتَابَهُ عَلَى بِنْتِ الْوَزِيرِ بِالْقَهْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-amara al-sulṭānu bi-iḥḍārihi wa-kataba kitābahu ʿalā binti al-wazīri bi-al-qahri
sentences.l: and-ordered the-Sultan the-bringing-of-him, and-he-wrote his-contract upon the-daughter-of the-vizier by-the-force.
sentences.i: The Sultan ordered him brought, and had his marriage contract written with the vizier's daughter, by force.
sentences.n: كَتَبَ كِتَابَهُ is "he drew up his (marriage) contract"; the "his" is the groom's.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَأَنْ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهَا فِي هَذِهِ اللَّيْلَةِ وَيَعْمَلَ لَهُ زِفَّةً
sentences.tr: wa-amara an yadkhula ʿalayhā fī hādhihi al-laylati wa-yaʿmala lahu zaffatan
sentences.l: and-he-ordered that he-enter upon-her in this the-night and-make for-him a-procession.
sentences.i: and he commanded that the groom go in to her that very night, and that a wedding procession be made for him.
sentences.n: The print runs وأمر أن together as وامران. يدخل عليها "enter upon her" is the plain idiom for consummating a marriage. زفة is the wedding procession that leads the bridegroom to the bride.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ تَرَكْتُهُ وَهُوَ بَيْنَ مَمَالِيكِ السُّلْطَانِ وَهُمْ وَاقِدُونَ الشُّمُوعَ حَوْلَهُ وَيَتَمَسْخَرُونَ عَلَيْهِ عَلَى بَابِ الْحَمَّامِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad taraktuhu wa-huwa bayna mamālīki al-sulṭāni wa-hum wāqidūna al-shumūʿa ḥawlahu wa-yatamaskharūna ʿalayhi ʿalā bābi al-ḥammāmi
sentences.l: and-already I-left-him, and-he among the-mamluks-of the-Sultan, and-they kindlers the-candles around-him, and-they-mock upon-him at the-door-of the-bathhouse.
sentences.i: I left him among the Sultan's mamluks, who were lighting candles around him and making a mockery of him at the door of the bathhouse.
sentences.n: واقدون with an object is odd, since the participle that takes one is مُوقِدُونَ; I have pointed what is printed, wāqidūna, "kindling". يتمسخرون is colloquial, from مَسْخَرَة "mockery".

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا بِنْتُ الْوَزِيرِ جَالِسَةٌ تَبْكِي بَيْنَ الدَّايَاتِ وَالْمَوَاشِطِ وَهِيَ أَشْبَهُ النَّاسِ بِهَذَا الشَّابِّ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā bintu al-wazīri jālisatun tabkī bayna al-dāyāti wa-al-mawāshiṭi wa-hiya ashbahu al-nāsi bi-hādhā al-shābbi
sentences.l: and-as-for the-daughter-of the-vizier, sitting, weeping, among the-nurses and-the-bridal-hairdressers, and-she most-like-of the-people to-this the-youth.
sentences.i: As for the vizier's daughter, she sits weeping among the nurses and the bridal attendants, and she is the one of all people most like this young man.
sentences.n: After أَمَّا the Classical text would have فَ before the predicate; here it is absent. الدايات are nurses or midwives, and المواشط are the women who dress and adorn the bride.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ رَسَمُوا عَلَى أَبِيهَا حَتَّى أَنَّهُ لَايَحْضُرُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qad rasamū ʿalā abīhā ḥattā annahu lā yaḥḍuruhā
sentences.l: and-already they-decreed upon her-father until that-he not attends-her.
sentences.i: And they have laid an order upon her father, so that he cannot attend her.
sentences.n: رسموا على is obscure to me: it seems to mean "put under orders" or "under guard", so that the father is kept away from his daughter. I have given the plain sense and I am not sure of it.

sentences.t: وَمَا رَأَيْتُ يَا أُخْتِي أَوْحَشَ مِنْ هَذَا الْأَحْدَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā raʾaytu yā ukhtī awḥasha min hādhā al-aḥdabi
sentences.l: and-not I-saw, O my-sister, more-hideous than this the-hunchback.
sentences.i: And I have never seen, my sister, anything uglier than this hunchback.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الصَّبِيَّةُ فَهِيَ أَحْسَنُ مِنْ هَذَا الشَّابِّ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-ṣabiyyatu fa-hiya aḥsanu min hādhā al-shābbi
sentences.l: and-as-for the-girl, she more-beautiful than this the-youth.
sentences.i: As for the girl, she is more beautiful even than this young man.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: and-overtook Shahrazād the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent and stopped her permitted speech.
sentences.n: The night ends in the usual rhyme, ṣabāḥ and mubāḥ.
